# **The Barber Institute of Fine Arts**

The Barber Institute of Fine Arts houses a leading art gallery and concert hall within its Grade-1 listed building, on the University of Birmingham’s Edgbaston campus. We use our internationally significant art collection and wide-ranging exhibition, music and public programmes to inspire and connect people.

@graph.name: The Barber Institute of Fine Arts
@graph.description: Monet, Manet, and Magritte; Renoir, Rubens, Rossetti and Rodin; Degas and Delacroix -- not to mention Picasso, Botticelli, Turner and Gainsborough... You can see major works by all these great artists in the Barber Institute of Fine Arts, at the University of Birmingham. There’s also a stunning coin gallery and an exciting programme of exhibitions, concerts, lectures, and family events.

[GARRY FABIAN MILLER: Between the Moon and the Hawthorn](https://www.ashmolean.org/exhibition/ashmolean-now-garry-fabian-miller)

### GARRY FABIAN MILLER: Between the Moon and the Hawthorn

This exhibition brings together two British artists separated by nearly two centuries, but united by a shared commitment to landscape, light, and the transformative power of place: contemporary artist Garry Fabian Miller and the 19th-century Romantic painter Samuel Palmer. Opens 26 Nov.

## Impressions of Light: 
Masterpieces from MuMa - Le Havre and The Bowes Museum

### 26 September 2026 - 14 March 2027

A major international partnership with the Musée d’Art moderne André Malraux (MuMa), Le Havre, brings Impressionist masterpieces from France to The Bowes Museum.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://thebowesmuseum.org.uk/exhibitions/impressions-of-light-masterpieces-from-muma-le-havre-and-the-bowes-museum/)

## Norman Cornish: A Life in Sketchbooks

### 27 June - 10 January

Step inside the working imagination of Norman Cornish in this intimate exhibition, bringing together finished drawings, paintings and watercolours alongside the preparatory sketches that shaped them.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://thebowesmuseum.org.uk/exhibitions/norman-cornish-a-life-in-sketchbooks/)

- ## BEN URI GALLERY AND MUSEUM

 ### **NOW OPEN**

 ### THE ABBEY ART CENTRE AS POSTWAR REFUGE

 #### UNTIL 18 December

 ### **EVERY WEDNESDAY-FRIDAY, 10 AM - 5:30 PM**

 ### **ADDRESS**

 108a Boundary Road,

 off Abbey Road,

 St John’s Wood, 
 London, 
 NW8 0RH

 ### **OPENING HOURS**

 Wednesday to Friday 10 am - 5.30 pm

 Registered in England 01488690

 Registered Charity 280389

- ## TRANSPORT/PARKING OPTIONS

 ### **BY RAIL**

 Underground stations, St Johns Wood, Swiss Cottage, Finchley Road and Maida Vale are all a 10 minutes’ walk away from the gallery. West Hampstead and Kilburn High Road London Overground stations are also within easy walking distance. We advise you to navigate your journey using the **[Transport for London (TfL)](https://tfl.gov.uk/ 'Transport for London (TfL) ')** site.  

 ### **By bus**

 Buses 189 and 139 stop at the junction off Abbey Road and Boundary Road. Bus 31 Stops at the junction off Belsize Road and Abbey Road, and then it is a short walk from Boundary Road. 16/32/98 to Kilburn High Road is also within easy walking distance. Go to Transport for London to plan your journey by rail or bus. We advise you to navigate your journey using the **[Transport for London (TfL)](https://tfl.gov.uk/ 'Transport for London (TfL) ')** site.  

 ### **Parking**

 There is metered car parking on both sides of Boundary Road. 

- ## ACCESSIBILITY

 We have a ramp to facilitate wheelchairs to the ground floor gallery – please ask. We regret that there is no access for wheelchair users or those with mobility difficulties to the lower ground floor, library and archive. However, we are always happy to show high-resolution images of all works displayed downstairs. 

 **[Our full Access Policy](https://benuri.org/usr/library/documents/policy-docs/bu-access-policy-2017.pdf)**

 If you have any special requirements, please contact the gallery at **[admin@benuri.org](mailto:admin@benuri.org)**

- ## PLENTY TO DO AROUND US

 Boundary Road offers a wide variety of cafés and restaurants. Within easy walking distance is the famous Beatles' Abbey Road Crossing and Abbey Road Studios, Regent’s Canal, Regents Park, London Zoo and the boutiques of St John’s Wood High Street. Nearby attractions include The Freud Museum, The Jewish Museum, The Sherlock Holmes Museum and Madame Tussauds.

# Courtauld Gallery

The Courtauld Gallery is home to one of the world’s great art collections, located in the magnificent historical setting of Somerset House in central London. Book your visit to see the Courtauld Gallery's much-loved collection of masterpieces ranging from the Middle Ages to the 20th century.

i The LVMH Great Room ©Hufton+Crow

The first solo exhibition in Europe of the celebrated New York-based painter Salman Toor, bringing together 19 of the artist’s most iconic, thought-provoking and at times humorous paintings, never-before-seen in Britain.

# A Call to Art: William Morris and the Pre-Raphaelites

23 October 2026 - 3 May 2027

[Book now](https://fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/plan-your-visit/exhibitions/a-call-to-art-william-morris-and-the-pre-raphaelites)

## Welcome to the Fitzwilliam Museum

Experience award-winning exhibitions, events and a changing display of artworks and objects from throughout history to today. From ancient Egyptian artefacts to modern and contemporary art, our eclectic collection has something for everyone.

[Plan your visit](https://fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/plan-your-visit)

### We're open

Closed

10am – 5pm

## Late Night Shopping

Stay late at the Fitz on Friday 27 November for a special evening viewing of 'A Call to Art: William Morris and the Pre-Raphaelites' and explore collection-inspired gifts in our shop.

[Find out more](https://fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/late-night-shopping)

## We're an Art Fund Museum of the Year finalist

We're thrilled to have made the shortlist for Art Fund's Museum of the Year award 2026, the world's largest museum prize.

[Find out more](https://www.fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/art-fund-s-museum-of-the-year)

## Future Legacies

Head to our new online platform and discover a community of Black artists, thinkers and creatives. From zines and soundscapes to articles, interviews and films each explores the concept of the ‘Black Atlantic’ through the art, music, writings and conversations.

[Explore now](https://futurelegacies.fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/)

## In the Collection

### Joseph Wright Gallery

Derby Museums is home to the world’s largest collection of works by Joseph Wright of Derby but his art also graces the walls of some of the most famous galleries, including The Hermitage in St Petersburg, New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art, Tate Britain, and the National Gallery of Victoria, Australia.

[View the Collection](https://www.derbymuseums.org/collection/joseph-wright-of-derby/)

## Secure our Heritage

## Artist Takeover

---

We are handing the Gallery over to the five Cornwall-based artists and collectives who were selected for our new Artist Takeover opportunity. We have supported them as they developed an innovative series of exhibitions and events for you to enjoy. Please be aware that the rooms will be closed between exhibitions. 

02 Oct 2026 - 09 Feb 2027 

[Find out more](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/events/artist-takeover)

### Free entry

Mon – Sat. 10 – 4pm 
Closed Sunday & Bank Holidays

## What’s on & what’s next

---

We have a vibrant and varying programme of exhibitions, collection displays, workshops, talks and events that has something for everyone to enjoy.

- [**Artist Takeover**](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/events/artist-takeover)

- [**An Evening of Storytelling and Shrine Making**](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/events/an-evening-of-storytelling-and-shrine-making)

### Where is Falmouth Art Gallery?

We are a free art gallery right in the heart of Falmouth on The Moor. We share our historic Municipal Building with the Town Library.

[Getting here](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/falmouthartgallery/your-visit/#getting-here)

### Gallery news

Read the latest Gallery news about recent acquisitions to our Collection and the 2026/26 Exhibitions programme.

[Latest Gallery news](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/falmouthartgallery/news)

Mary Winifred Freeman

## Explore our Collections

Raphaelites

### Our Collections

Encompassing broad ranging artforms and ever-evolving, our outstanding collection reflects Falmouth’s rich cultural heritage and communities.

[Explore our collections](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/falmouthartgallery/featured-collections/)

### Falmouth’s Automata archive

In 2018 Falmouth Art Gallery staged a Heritage Lottery Funded Project entitled ‘A Cabaret of Mechanical Movement’ to capture and celebrate the town’s automata-making heritage.

[The home of Automata](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/falmouthartgallery/featured-collections/automata-in-falmouth)

### Surrealism in Cornwall

Explore our collection of surrealist artists within Falmouth.

[The Collection](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/falmouthartgallery/featured-collections/the-surrealists-in-cornwall)

### RCPS Tuke Collection

The RCPS Tuke Collection is currently on long loan to Falmouth Art Gallery. The Tuke collection is believed to be unique. These works will be made available for exhibitions at a local, national and international level.

[Find out more about the Tuke Collection](https://www.falmouthtowncouncil.co.uk/falmouthartgallery/featured-collections/rcps-tuke-collection/)

Browse our range of unique gifts inspired by our art collection. Your purchase will help support the Gallery. All products are made sustainably in the UK.

**Welcome to The Armitt** – a museum, gallery, and library full of interesting and unusual objects telling the history and heritage of Ambleside, its people, and the surrounding Lake District landscape. Tickets to visit the museum and exhibitions can be booked online via the website or alternatively at the museum’s visitor reception. Please explore our online content and we look forward to welcoming you and helping you explore the heritage of the Lakeland world.

[BOOK GENERAL ADMISSION TICKETS](https://www.armitt.com/visiting/)

EXHIBITIONS

CLUB CULTURE CUMBRIA

[LEARN MORE](https://www.armitt.com/club-culture-cumbria/)

MODERN-DAY MARTINEAU

[LEARN MORE](https://www.armitt.com/modern-day-martineau-2/)

AN A–Z OF BEATRIX POTTER

[LEARN MORE](https://www.armitt.com/an-a-z-of-beatrix-potter/)





#### HELP US MEET OUR GOAL

The Armitt is delighted to have been awarded a share in the latest round of the Museum Estate and Development fund (MEND) to support essential improvements to our heating, ventilation and air conditioning system. We need to match 5% of the total amount through our own fundraising, meaning we are on a mission to raise £13,000.

Anything you give will allow visitors to continue to enjoy our collection of over 70,000 Lake District objects, including Beatrix Potter’s fungi watercolours, paintings by the avant-garde artist Kurt Schwitters, and archaeology from the Ambleside Roman Fort.

We hope you’ll consider giving a donation today to help us reach our goal.

[DONATE HERE](https://www.paypal.com/donate?campaign_id=89SM4N666NJDE)

The Collections

**Archaeology 
**Nestled in the valleys, mountain ranges, and on the coastlines of Cumbria are ancient artifacts, giving us a glimpse into the lives of past peoples. These artifacts are pieces of archaeology. The Armitt holds over 1000 of such archaeological items in its collection ranging from prehistoric items to objects from the Roman occupation of Ambleside from the first to the fourth centuries.

**Kurt Schwitters 
**German-born artist Kurt Schwitters settled in Ambleside in 1945. Many of his paintings are now in The Armitt’s collection, including Silver Howe, Bowl of Flowers, and Dr Johnston. Find out more about the artist and his works here.

**The Armitt Sisters 
**The Armitt was named for, and after, Mary Louisa Armitt who wished that there would be “a place for academic and booklovers and eventually a museum might be made that should illustrate the life of Ambleside, through the long past to the present”. Discover the Armitt sisters’ story.

[CHARLOTTE-MASON](https://www.armitt.com/charlotte-mason/)

**Charlotte Mason 
**Charlotte Mason (1842-1923) established her House of Education in Ambleside in 1892. Her friend Selina Healey whom she had met at college in London in 1860 lived there, and Charlotte often visited. She thought Ambleside was an ideal place to set up her training institution for governesses.

[Beatrix Potter](https://www.armitt.com/beatrix-potter/)

**Beatrix Potter 
**Few people are more embedded in the Lake District than writer and artist Beatrix Potter (1866-1943). She is world famous for her beloved children’s books, but she achieved a great deal more in her life. Learn about her scientific ambitions, her watercolours of fungi and archaeological artefacts, her involvement in Cumbrian farming, and much more…

EXPLORE MORE . . .

# What's On

With [Christmas](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/christmas/) right around the corner, get into the festive spirit with our magical trails, visits to meet Father Christmas or try your hands at seasonal crafts.

Follow our [Walking with The Snowman™ trail at Belsay Hall and Wrest Park](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/#section3), have some [Festive Fun](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/#section5) or make the season extra special with a visit to [meet Father Christmas](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/#section4).

Make a start on your Christmas shopping and [find a Christmas Market to visit](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/#section7), or get creative and join us for one of our [Wreath-making workshops](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/#section6).

Plus, celebrate the [Winter Solstice at Stonehenge](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/#section8).

There's plenty to do at English Heritage sites in the run-up to Christmas.

_Don't forget, if you book your tickets to our daytime events in advance, you can **save 15%** on your entry price._

## Walking with The Snowman™ Christmas Trail

This winter, something special is happening at Wrest Park and Belsay Hall, Castle and Gardens. The Snowman™ has tip‑toed into the gardens – and he’s brought a host of cheerful friends with him.

From Saturday 7 November follow a festive family trail to discover twelve giant Snowman sculptures hidden throughout the grounds, inspired by Raymond Briggs' beloved classic.

Keep your eyes peeled – each sculpture hides a secret letter. Collect all twelve and you’ll reveal a magical Christmas word.

So pull on your hats and scarves and head out for a charming winter adventure, sprinkled with nostalgia from Raymond Briggs’ much‑loved classic.

- **[Book your visit to Belsay Hall, Castle and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/505609a6df7f4c5b8de3da9534d92209.aspx)**
- **[Book your visit to Wrest Park](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/456e3dd392a64f1c8afb01ee1b9c6bdb.aspx)**

_Book in advance online and save 15%. Members go free._

## Book your visit to meet Father Christmas

Join Father Christmas at one of our historical sites this December for a magical way to start the festive season. After a group storytelling session, you and your children will meet the man himself, with the chance to take photographs and make memories to treasure and recieve a traditional present to unwrap.

- **[Meet Father Christmas at Audley And House and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/1eb2608aafb54304aced53db7309e8b8.aspx), Saffron Walden**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Belsay Hall, Castle and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/33b8b5930b0c4ff18b8483fe58b419a0.aspx), Northumberland**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Brodsworth Hall and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/e7ffd3b8c81c41c3aa83e7837ad2ca9e.aspx), Doncaster**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Dover Castle](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/2228e81b828b43968595de99cf705f91.aspx), Dover**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Eltham Palace and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/dd132dba460c476db0cc019e868bca86.aspx), London**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Kenilworth Castle and Elizabethan Garden](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/f21849d8c3804d5092e3055359f6d7b6.aspx), Warwickshire**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Kenwood](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/ce2664d764994d9e87e537858cf3c576.aspx), London**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Marble Hill](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/b36a029709d04ef4a8f95812b3993f2b.aspx), London**
- **[Meet Father Christmas at Wrest Park](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/d996455711cb4d87bfc358012655b694.aspx), Bedfordshire**

## Have some Festive Fun

Join us for festive days out across the country that the whole family will love. Follow Christmas-themed trails around our historic grounds and make magical memories along the way.

Plus, try your hand at some Christmas-themed crafts.

**Book your visit for:**

- **[Festive Fun at Audley And House and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/8458ecb26d76442fbc67468f6405deff.aspx), Saffron Walden**
- **[Festive Fun at Belsay Hall, Castle and Gardens](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/adebccc9932d40a1aa3dd5c00d986a79.aspx), Northumberland**

- **[Festive Fun at Kenilworth Castle and Elizabethan Garden](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/bee631a08e35451da2c43fa4e566de80.aspx), Warwickshire**

_Book in advance online and save 15%. Members go free._

## Enjoy a Wreath-making Workshop

Join us in magnificent surroundings for a fabulously festive day of wreath making. You will be guided through the step by step process by our expert gardeners to create a beautiful wreath. Book a workshop at:

- [**Audley End House and Gardens, Essex**](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/af01366a01fd457fb85bafc9f5ec7156.aspx) (includes a Festive Afternoon Tea)
- [**Eltham Palace and Gardens, London**](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/a2204eb5affc4e2aaf3e80a2cdb01a31.aspx) (includes a Festive Afternoon Tea)
- [**Marble Hill, London**](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/e64b3f78489b4922af3bf628f1f5396f.aspx)
- [**Wrest Park, Bedfordshire**](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/link/99b54392eb2940d29af34eeed26d0c68.aspx) (includes a Festive Afternoon Tea)

## Christmas Markets to visit

Discover some of the best Christmas markets and festive fairs to visit at English Heritage sites this winter.

Browse stalls filled with unique gifts, handmade crafts and seasonal treats, all set against the backdrop of our stunning historic castles, houses and grounds.

Whether you're looking for the perfect present or want to get into the festive spirit, there's something for everyone to enjoy.

[Find a Christmas Market to visit](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/whats-on/christmas-markets/)

## Winter Solstice 2026

Stonehenge was built to align with the sun on the solstices. This remarkable feat is celebrated each year in Summer and Winter. This year, you can join us on Tuesday 22 December, or catch our livestreams on [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/c/EnglishHeritage) and [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/englishheritage/?locale=en_GB).

This iconic monument is the perfect place to mark the longest day of the year.

You must pre-book parking if choosing not to travel to Stonehenge by public transport.

[Find out more about Winter Solstice](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/visit/places/stonehenge/things-to-do/solstice/winter-solstice-2026/)

## Members' Events

Exclusively for you, our Members' Events offer behind-the-scenes access to our sites and expert tours. From London walking tours to experiencing how Christmas at a country house was celebrated, you can get up and close to heritage with our historians.

Bookings are now open for Members’ Events taking place from October 2026 through to March 2027. Browse all the events on offer and book your tickets now. Spaces are limited

[Explore all Members' Events](https://www.english-heritage.org.uk/members-area/members-events/)

## 5-star membership. Explore over 400 historic sites

Join today and enjoy unlimited historic days out across over 400 sites for the entire year and with free kids entry, there’s no better time to join and start making new memories all year round.

Plus your support for us as a charity means you're helping to protect heritage sites for generations to come.

# Dorich House Museum

## The extraordinary 1930s studio-home of Dora Gordine and Richard Hare

Open Thursday to Saturday, 11am–5pm 
FREE ENTRY

[Plan your visit](https://www.dorichhousemuseum.org.uk/visit/)

## Welcome

Dorich House Museum is located a ‘deer’s leap’ from Richmond Park on Kingston Vale in South West London.

The house is the 1930s former studio-home of the artist Dora Gordine and her husband the Hon. Richard Hare.  They named their home Do-rich for Dora and Richard.  The museum holds the largest collection of Gordine’s work and the couple’s Russian art collection.

We are open to the public from Thursday to Saturday.  Self-guided visits are free to all and you do not need to book to visit.  Guided tours cost £5 per person and should be booked in advance.  To book, please see below.

If you are a member of our Kingston University community, please see ‘Get Involved’ for information on how we support staff and students.

[Visit](https://www.dorichhousemuseum.org.uk/visit/) [Book a guided tour](https://www.dorichhousemuseum.org.uk/visit/#section-5) [Get Involved](https://www.dorichhousemuseum.org.uk/get-involved/)

## Cookies Statement

Explains what information we will collect about you, what cookies are and how we use your information.

### What are cookies?

A cookie is a small text file that resides on your computer. Cookies are used to remember your settings when you revisit a website and to identify how visitors navigate the site. Cookies provide valuable information to website owners to adapt and make changes to the site in order to improve the user experience.

Cookies are anonymous and contain no personal data. If you never register or leave personal information at a site, the only confirmation they give is that you are a returning visitor. The cookie will only contain information that you freely provide to a website.

#### Types of cookies

Cookies tend to be one, or a combination of, the following types:

##### Session cookies

Files that allow a site to link the actions of a visitor during a single browser session. These might be used by an internet bank or webmail service. They are not stored long term and are considered "less privacy intrusive" than persistent cookies.

##### Persistent cookies

These remain on the user's device between sessions and allow one or several sites to remember details about the visitor. They may be used by marketers to target advertising or to avoid the user having to provide a password each visit.

##### First and third-party cookies

A cookie is classed as being first-party if it is set by the site being visited. It might be used to study how people navigate a site.

It is classed as third-party if it is issued by a different server to that of the domain being visited. It could be used to trigger a banner advert based on the visitor's viewing habits.

You can read more about cookies on the [All About Cookies website (Opens in new tab or window)](https://www.allaboutcookies.org/)

### Why do you use cookies?

When people visit any of the East Riding of Yorkshire Council's websites we collect some standard internet usage information, and details of visitor behaviour patterns. This is done to learn how customers use our sites, to help us improve them.

We collect this data in a way which does not identify anyone. We do not make any attempt to find out the identities of those visiting our websites (unless you have previously approved us to do so). We will not associate any data gathered from these sites with any personally identifying information from any source.

If we want to collect personally identifiable information through our website, we will tell you beforehand. We will make it clear when we collect this information and will explain what we intend to do with.

### How can I control your cookies on my computer?

You can control your cookie preferences for this site on the [Settings](https://www.eastridingmuseums.co.uk/) tab.

#### More about controlling cookies

Most web browsers also allow some control of most cookies through the browser settings. You can find out more about cookies, including how to see what cookies have been set and how to manage and delete them, on the [All About Cookies website (Opens in new tab or window)](https://www.allaboutcookies.org/)

| \_hjIncludedInPageviewSample | **Summary**<br>Hotjar<br>**Type**<br>session<br>**Expires**<br>30 mins<br>**What it does**<br>Set to determine if a user is included in the data sampling defined by your site's pageview limit.<br>**Additional information**<br>[Find out more about the **\_hjIncludedInPageviewSample** cookie](https://help.hotjar.com/hc/en-us/articles/115011789248-Hotjar-Cookie-Information)<br>**Is it necessary?**<br>No, however used for statistics and feedback. |
| \_hjSessionUser\_# | **Summary**<br>Hotjar<br>**Type**<br>session<br>**Expires**<br>1 year<br>**What it does**<br>Stores unique site user ID to allow data to be attributed to the same user.<br>**Additional information**<br>[Find out more about the **\_hjSessionUser\_#** cookie](https://help.hotjar.com/hc/en-us/articles/115011789248-Hotjar-Cookie-Information)<br>**Is it necessary?**<br>No, however used for statistics and feedback. |
| \_ga | **Summary**<br>Google Analytics<br>**Type**<br>session<br>**Expires**<br>2 years<br>**What it does**<br>To identify unique users<br>**Is it necessary?**<br>No, however used for statistics. |
| \_gid | **Summary**<br>Google Analytics<br>**Type**<br>session<br>**Expires**<br>1 day<br>**What it does**<br>To identify unique users<br>**Is it necessary?**<br>No, however used for statistics and feedback. |

# Hepworth Wakefield

## Open Tuesday - Sunday, 10am - 4pm. Café open from 9.30am. Exhibition entry is £6 / £5 from 3 - 20 November. FREE for Members, Wakefield District residents and under 18s.

The Hepworth Wakefield Festive market returns this November [— Read more](https://hepworthwakefield.org/whats-on/festive-market-2026/)

[Hokusai: Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji from the Iuchi Collection](https://www.dulwichpicturegallery.org.uk/whats-on/hokusai-thirty-six-views-of-mt-fuji-from-the-iuchi-collection/)

Exhibition

### Hokusai: Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji from the Iuchi Collection

20 Oct 2026 — 17 Jan 2027

3 Nov 2026 – 7 Feb 2027

2 Feb 2027 — 9 May 2027

### [Bushey Museum & Art Gallery](https://busheymuseum.org/# 'Bushey Museum & Art Gallery')

Bushey Museum and Art Gallery tells the story of Bushey and its unique artistic history.

### History of Bushey

Bushey local history from earliest times with displays of archaeology, artefacts, documents and historical maps.

### Sir Hubert von Herkomer, CVO RA

A nationally significant collection of art, artefacts and ephemera relating to the prominent portrait and genre painter.

### [Lucy Kemp-Welch](https://busheymuseum.org/# 'Lucy Kemp-Welch')

She was the foremost painter of horses of her time, and best known for her illustrations for Black Beauty by Anna Sewell.

##### _**Visit England 'Hidden Gem' 2025-2026 Award**_

Bushey Museum's Val Penketh, our office manager, and Hannah Schoenholtz, our art curator, receiving the Museum's second Hidden Gem accolade in as many years at the Visit England awards lunch.

We recently had our annual, unannounced Visit England Assessment and once again we passed with flying colours! For the second year running, we have been nominated for a “Hidden Gem” award - and we have been advised that it is unusual to receive this accolade in two consecutive years! The Herkomer Portraits and Off the Wall exhibitions were both commended, as were the “very approachable and helpful” Stewards, who on this occasion were Irene Simonaro and Meg Flanigan. The Museum building itself also received compliments, with maintenance standards adjudged to be very good, while we got 100% for Cleanliness. Here credit is due to our Buildings Manager Dave Berry and our long-serving cleaner Judy Bentley. Both Dave and Judy take great pride in their work at the Museum, and it is fitting that their efforts are recognised. 
_November 2026_

**_PETITION - PLEASE SIGN - click on picture left for link._**

#### **_We now have nearly 2,000 signatures!_**

The aim of our **Petition** is:

#### _**“To prevent the Council relocating Bushey Museum & Art Gallery from Rudolph Road to the proposed community hub planned at the Bushey Country Club development”.**_

Ever since Hertsmere Borough Council announced they had signed off on the redevelopment of the Bushey Golf Club site in August 2025, the future of Bushey Museum & Art Gallery has been thrown into serious doubt.

We, the Friends of Bushey Museum (Registered Charity no: 1039713), are spearheading a petition to be presented to Hertsmere Borough Council.

The Museum is under threat of being removed from its home of more three decades - the former Bushey Urban District Council Offices in the heart of Bushey village Conservation Area. The Museum holds the largest collection of public artworks in Hertfordshire, including artworks by 19th century portraitist and polymath, Sir Hubert von Herkomer (1849-1914), and students of his famous Bushey Art School, notably Lucy Kemp-Welch (1869-1958). The Museum has formally dedicated two complete galleries to Herkomer and Kemp-Welch.

**The proposed plan** is to build 286 homes within a community complex. The scheme includes a supermarket, car park, and a ‘modern community and cultural hub’ containing an early years’ facility, a café, library and an ‘art gallery’. The first public consultation revealed a vague, artist’s impression of a modern, white building with no real indication of actual size or interior layout. It looks likely that the Museum will be rehoused in a template ‘white box’ without the necessary storage space for the entirety of its vast collection of art and heritage objects. This would simply not allow for future expansion, which is inevitable, as it would include the works of both traditional and contemporary Bushey artists. The proposed relocation will incur considerable costs and result in a significant upheaval.

We later discovered that the architects had based their initial plan for the gallery on a previous,  modern museum design. The proposal clearly shows their ignorance or complete misunderstanding of the Museum and its contents, its unique location and setting. And its long-established, active role in conserving and promoting the artistic, historic and cultural heritage of Bushey and its community.

The Friends of Bushey Museum say the proposed plan is ill-conceived and totally out of context for the following key reasons:

- Historical
- Cultural
- Practical
- Financial
- Aesthetic

We call on Hertsmere Borough Council to stop their plan to relocate Bushey Museum & Art Gallery from Rudolph Road to the proposed community hub planned at the Bushey Country Club development.This petition has been organised with the approval of the Chairman and the Trustees of Bushey Museum.

##### _**Click [here](https://www.change.org/p/stop-the-move-now) to sign the Petition.**_

     _Kelvin Graham,  Petition Starter_

##### _**Social Media**_

Apart from lots of information on this website, we also have lots of interesting posts on other social media sites. Click on the links below to find out more!

[Accredited by the Arts council, England](https://www.artscouncil.org.uk/supporting-arts-museums-and-libraries/museums-accreditation-scheme)        [Link to the Art UK website](https://artuk.org/visit/venues/bushey-museum-and-art-gallery-3581)              [Link to Hertsmere Borough Council website](https://www.hertsmere.gov.uk/parks-and-leisure/museums-and-theatres/bushey-museum-and-art-gallery)            [Link to the Bushey Museum page on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/busheymuseumandartgallery)

### **About [Us](https://www.ticketsource.co.uk/friends-of-bushey-museum)**

_Bushey Museum Trust is a Charitable Incorporated Organisation - more information below._

**_Address_ 
**Bushey Museum & Art Gallery 
Rudolph Road, Bushey, Hertfordshire, WD23 3HW

_**Entry 
**_**Free!** Donations are always welcome! 

**_Phone_ 
****Museum - 020 8950 3233 
**Opening times: 
Thursday - Sunday  11.00 am - 4.00 pm. **Office - 020 8420 4057 
**Opening times: 
Wednesday - Friday  10.00 am - 4.00 pm. 

The [**Visit Us**](https://busheymuseum.org/visit-us/) page tells you how to get to the Museum. 
The [**About Us**](https://busheymuseum.org/about-us/) page gives you more about the history of the Museum and what we have to offer. 
The [**What’s On**](https://busheymuseum.org/current-exhibitions/) page includes details of all of our current Exhibitions.

_**Car Parking**_ 
**On site** There is some car parking on site, no cost: you’ll have to approach from the bottom of Rudolph Road (a one way street) and enter the car park just before the Museum building. It may of course be full! 
**On roads** There is also some parking on the local roads, but limited parking times: do see the signs! 
**Kemp Place** Across the High Street is the Kemp Place car park. Up to 1 hour is £1.15. For the cost of longer parking click [**_here_**.](https://www.hertsmere.gov.uk/transport-streets-and-parking/parking-in-hertsmere/car-parks/kemp-place)

###### **Who are we?**

The **Bushey Museum & Art Gallery** in Bushey, Hertfordshire has a local history collection, plus a major art collection spanning 200 years, with paintings, prints and drawings, sculpture, Bushey Heath lustre pottery and historic church silver as well as costume and embroidery.

The Museum has a unique artistic history - which is of national significance - and it majors on **[Sir Hubert von Herkomer RA](https://busheymuseum.org/herkomer-room/)** with works of art, artefacts and ephemera relating to him and his famous Art School in Bushey. There is also a major collection of paintings by Herkomer's student **[Lucy Kemp-Welch](https://busheymuseum.org/lcw-gallery/),** as well as works by other artists drawn to Bushey by its artistic reputation.

Art UK say on their website: "...the art collection is the largest in Hertfordshire and is mainly from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, with special interest in the Monro Circle of artists, Sir Hubert von Herkomer, Lucy Kemp-Welch and the pupils of their Art Schools and other Bushey art schools."

Located in an Edwardian former Council building close to Bushey High Street, it features galleries with displays of local history; Herkomer and Lucy Kemp-Welch paintings and memorabilia, as well as other Galleries with changing displays, see [**What's-On**](https://busheymuseum.org/current-exhibitions/).

Click on **[Museum Shop](https://busheymuseum.org/museum-shop/)** to see the wide range of local history books, greetings cards featuring local artists' pictures - and much more - which can be bought in the Shop at the Museum, or via this website. And there is also a link to the Art UK website (see below as well) where you can buy prints of over 120 paintings from our Collection. Well worth a look!

There is a **[Meeting Room](https://busheymuseum.org/meeting-room/)** which is available for hire to local societies or individuals for meetings, talks, etc.

###### **Arts Council England**

Bushey Museum and Art Gallery has **Full Accreditation** status with the Arts Council England (RD 1048). Visit their site [**here**](http://www.artscouncil.org.uk).

###### **Art UK**

Bushey Museum and Art Gallery is an **Art UK Founder Partner**. Visit their website **[here](https://artuk.org/visit/venues/bushey-museum-and-art-gallery-3581)** to see over 1000 of the paintings in our collection! And also visit their **Art UK Shop** **[here](https://artuk.org/shop/prints/filter/bushey-museum-and-art-gallery/_/7082.html?showall=1#PCF-15933)**where you can buy prints of over 120 of the pictures in our collection!

###### **Charity Commission**

Bushey Museum Trust is a registered charity with the Charity Commission in England and Wales No. 294261.

###### **Charitable Incorporated Organisation**

In April 2023 the Museum successfully transitioned from a Charitable Company Limited by Guarantee to become a Charitable Incorporated Organisation, saving many hours of work and simplifying the administration, particularly all that connected with preparing, examining and submitting the annual accounts.

**© 2026, Bushey Museum Trust, a Charitable Incorporated Organisation. Charity number: 1109042.**

##### **Current Exhibitions**

_**Creature Feature**_

## 

_Until 3rd January 2027 
__Council Chamber_

This brings together a selection of paintings, illustrations and other artworks, all by Bushey artists, that represent a variety of animal and bird life, domestic and wild. _**[More](https://busheymuseum.org/council-chamber/)**_

**_Anthony Wildig - a landscape painter_** 
_From 17th October 2026 to 11th April 2027_

Anthony’s working life as antique furniture restorer and cabinet maker has kept him busy. Painting has always been part of that life and time has shown watercolour to be his preferred medium. 
An interest in architecture and a love for the wide variety of landscape found throughout Britain has been his inspiration for much of his work. Visits to Cornwall and The Outer Hebrides, both more remote and barren places, have had great appeal. 
This exhibition shows paintings going back over a period of time, some from Bushey Museum Trust Collection, others on loan, and his most recent work. A selection of his paintings are available for sale. 
For more details of Anthony and for many of his paintings click [**_here_**](https://busheymuseum.org/artists-anthony-wildig/).

**_St Hilda's School Exhibition_** 
_Jubilee Room 
From 3rd September_

## 

When St Hilda's School closed last year the Museum was entrusted with the school's archive material. We will show some of the photographs and items of interest as we explore the origins of the house, the life of the School and its founder Miss Violet Curry ,who shaped the school from the beginning. Our Exhibition reflects her love of nature and the importance she gave to lessons outside the classroom, which continued at St Hilda's until it closed. We have her extraordinary personal journals which are beautifully illustrated with watercolour pictures of the natural world. We will be telling stories of the man who built the original house and the famous people who have been linked to the school. This is an opportunity to see how the school began and evolved over time. _Click [here](https://busheymuseum.org/st-hilda/) to see the poster full size._

##### **Future Exhibitions**

Click _[**here**](https://busheymuseum.org/future-exhibition/)._

##### **Local Bushey History 
**

_Ground floor galleries 
_The gallery gives a social history of Bushey with maps, extracts of medieval documents, and some ancient artefacts. It includes local industries, schools, police and fire brigade history, the World Wars, transport, celebrities, and more! _**[More.](https://busheymuseum.org/local-history-galleries/)**_

This gallery also includes a collection of **Bushey Heath Pottery,** for more information, click [_**here**_](https://busheymuseum.org/bushey-heath-pottery/).

##### [**Hubert von Herkomer - paintings & memorabilia**](https://busheymuseum.org/herkomer-room/)

_Hubert von Herkomer Gallery_

The life, work and castle of Sir Hubert von Herkomer RA, also his School of Art, and including some of his most notable paintings. _**[More.](https://busheymuseum.org/herkomer-room/)**_

###### _**A Herkomer painting not seen in public for 100 years is on display!**_

['The Lady in White' by Herkomer](https://busheymuseum.org/the-lady-in-white/)The Museum was delighted when it recently acquired this unique Herkomer painting! Almost all of Herkomer's portaits were of men, but in 1885 he produced this portrait of Miss Katherine Grant - the painting known as 'The Lady in White'. Come and see it in the Herkomer Gallery. For more about this impressive painting, click [_**here**_](https://busheymuseum.org/the-lady-in-white/)!

Click [_**here**_](https://busheymuseum.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Volunteers-Handbook.pdf) to download this leaflet (pdf, 9.8MB)

##### **Art Curators**

The Museum has many volunteers carrying out many roles, not least our _**Art Curators.**_ Click [**_here_**](https://busheymuseum.org/art-curators/) to find out more about them!

##### **Donations of Bushey-related artefacts**

Our Curator of Social History said "I am very aware that, in contrast to when I started volunteering at Bushey Museum and Art Gallery some 17 years ago, we are not receiving a regular flow of donations of Bushey-related artefacts to display in the new 'recent arrivals' case. Items should have been used in Bushey or are related to Bushey, or with costumes it should be items which could have been worn in Bushey. Should you have anything you are happy to donate we shall be delighted to consider it. The sort of items are pottery, china, costume articles, books, pictures, records etc., and many others. These can be left with the stewards on duty and you will be informed as soon as possible if we would like to add them to the Museum's collection." 
Tony Woollard.

### _**Bushey Restaurants**_

Click on the poster below to see a larger poster with details of 13 restaurants in Bushey! Enjoy!

###### _**Bushey Museum Jigsaws!**_

Fancy doing an online jigsaw? Just click on the picture... enjoy! And click _**[here](https://busheymuseum.org/jigsaws/)**_  to see more jigsaws!

[Ploughing by Algernon Talmage](https://www.jigsawplanet.com/?rc=play&pid=18860783668d)

Ploughing by Algernon Talmage

### Visit Us

**_Address_** 
**Bushey Museum and Art Gallery** 
**Rudolph Road** 
**Bushey** 
**Hertfordshire   WD23 3HW**

**_Opening times 
_**Thursday – Sunday, 11.00am – 4.00pm.

**_Phone_** 
**Galleries 020 8950 3233** Thu-Sun 11am-4pm. 
**Office 020 8420 4057** Wed-Fri 10am-4pm.

### About This Site

**For more information on the Museum’s Privacy Policy click [here](https://busheymuseum.org/privacy-policy/).**

**This site regularly maintained, and feedback for new content and updates is always welcome: please email Andrew Gunton at webmaster @ busheymuseum.org (no spaces).**

### Exciting hire opportunity at Gainsborough’s House!

Looking for a unique space to showcase your work, test a new idea or connect with new audiences? Our Creative Brief booklet gives you everything you need to know about bringing creative projects to Gainsborough’s House, from exhibitions and workshops to retail pop-ups and collaborative programmes.

Set within one of Suffolk’s leading cultural venues, this is a chance to be part of a vibrant creative destination in the heart of Sudbury and share your work with thousands of visitors each year.

We send a monthly newsletter along with quarterly round-ups of our upcoming events and exhibitions via email. Get all the latest news from Gainsborough’s House straight to your inbox!

## Your donations matter

We are a small, dynamic organisation with ambitious plans for the future. We wish to be able to show more of Gainsborough’s masterpieces, provide more opportunities for people to enjoy and appreciate art and social history, and help generate economic success in Sudbury. With your help, we can put Sudbury, and the region of Suffolk, firmly on the global, cultural map. Your support at this time is invaluable.

However you choose to donate, we thank you for helping us raise money for our charity. Please click the ‘Donate now’ button below to make an online donation.

Please contact us [mail@gainsborough.org](mailto:mail@gainsborough.org) if you would like to make a regular gift donation via Direct Debit.

### About Gainsborough’s House

Thomas Gainsborough (1727–88) was born in Sudbury and baptised at the Independent Meeting-House in Friars Street on 14 May 1727, the fifth son and ninth child of John and Mary Gainsborough. In 1958, Gainsborough’s House Society was formed to purchase the house and establish it as a centre for Thomas Gainsborough. The Museum opened to the public in 1961 and has remained open for over 50 years. The beautiful historic garden at the heart of Gainsborough’s House is maintained by a devoted body of volunteers. In November 2022, the museum re-opened to the public after a transformational refurbishment. The international centre for Thomas Gainsborough is now the largest gallery in Suffolk.

# Nature in Art Museum and Art Gallery

### **OPENING HOURS: Tuesday – Sunday 10am – 5pm.**

**Find us 2m north of Gloucester on A38. SatNav Postcode: GL2 9PG. Follow the Nature in Art brown tourism signs.**

**Our Hayward Coffee shop is open the same hours**. Non museum visitors welcome. 

## Welcome to Nature in Art, the world’s first museum and art gallery dedicated to fine, decorative and applied art inspired by nature.

s

Our unrivalled collection is housed in a fine Georgian mansion, featured in Simon Jenkins’s book ‘England’s 1000 Best Houses’, just outside the famous cathedral city of Gloucester. This website gives you a glimpse of Nature in Art, its collections and exhibitions, and the extensive programme of events and activities that take place throughout the year.

[See Our Calendar of Events](https://natureinart.org.uk/whatson/) [About Nature in Art](https://natureinart.org.uk/about/) [Visitor Information](https://natureinart.org.uk/visit/) [The Nature in Art Collection](https://natureinart.org.uk/collection/) [Have a Go at Nature in Art](https://natureinart.org.uk/haveago/) [Young People at Nature in Art](https://natureinart.org.uk/youngpeople/) [Artists at work videos](https://natureinart.org.uk/artists-demonstrating-video/) [Explore the Collection](https://natureinart.org.uk/collection-spotlights/)

This Week

- **Special Exhibition: October 20th – November  15th: [Wild](https://natureinart.org.uk/whatson/action~agenda/cat_ids~20/request_format~json/)** Contemporary Crafts by The Cotswold Craftsmen.
- **Special Exhibition:** **November 10th – December 13th: [Nicholas Jones: Aurora](https://natureinart.org.uk/event/aurora/?instance_id=1076)**
- ****Artists in Residence:**** **10th – 15th November: A different member of [COTSWOLD CRAFTSMEN](http://www.cotswold-craftsmen.org) each day** _These are last artists in residence of 2026! Don’t miss them!_

###### **[Looking Deep into Nature](https://natureinart.org.uk/event/looking-deep-into-nature/?instance_id=1074)** ended October 25th.       **[In Sync: Words and Wonders](https://natureinart.org.uk/event/in-sync-words-and-wonders/?instance_id=1073) ended October 4th    [2026 British Wildlife Photography Awards](https://natureinart.org.uk/event/british-wildlife-photography-awards-2/?instance_id=1100) ended Sept 6th.     [100 Years of Winchcombe Pottery](https://natureinart.org.uk/event/100-years-of-winchcombe-pottery/?instance_id=1072)  ended Aug 23rd.**

#### Nature in Art has no ongoing or guaranteed public or private funding and relies on its activities and visitors to maintain its vibrant programme of events, its collections and buildings

### “Who would have thought I should ever be President of the Royal Academy, or be knighted by the King? “What a go !” as an Essex farmer friend wrote to me in a letter.” – Alfred Munnings

## Royal Patronage

### **Her Majesty Queen Camilla has accepted an invitation to become Royal Patron of the Munnings Art Museum**

##### (October 2026) The Trustees and Director of the Munnings Art Museum are delighted to announce that following the visit by Their Majesties King Charles III and Queen Camilla in February, The Queen has accepted an invitation to become the museum’s first Royal Patron. 

Chairman, James Johnston said: “Her Majesty’s patronage is a wonderful affirmation of our ongoing work to engage people with the museum’s world-class collection. This wouldn’t be possible without the hard work and dedication of everyone involved with the museum.”. 

Jenny Hand, Museum Director, added “Violet Munnings was the driving force behind opening the museum in 1961 and it is as much her legacy as it is that of her husband. She would be delighted with the news of our Royal Patronage. It is a wonderful way to conclude our 65th anniversary year celebrations and offers motivation for the future.”.

### Available to buy: 

Christmas cards, Pack of 10 (2 x 5 designs) and individual cards 
Munnings Art Museum 2027 calendar 

[Shop Christmas >>](https://www.munningsmuseum.org.uk/product-category/christmas/)

##### **YOU TUBE** – **New to the Munnings Art Museum’s You Tube Channel** 

Sitting alongside our “At Home with Munnings” podcast is a series of short videos about the paintings featured in the podcast episodes. 

[To watch please follow this link >>](https://www.youtube.com/@munningsartmuseum1961)

##### **PODCAST – At Home with Munnings** 

Produced by our volunteer engagement team we are delighted to present our brand new podcast series “At Home with Munnings”. 

Episodes 1, 2 and 3 available now exploring three paintings by Sir Alfred Munnings, “Path to the Orchard”, “Tagg’s Island” and “Does the Subject Matter?” >> [PLAY EPISODES](https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/at-home-with-munnings-podcast/id1896934779) 

Listen on your usual podcast provider just search for “At Home with Munnings”.

## About the Art Museum

### **A home which houses t****he only permanent retrospective of paintings by Sir Alfred Munnings**

Each April to October the walls of the museum, Sir Alfred Munnings’ former home, Castle House, are sumptuously adorned with well-known pictures and lesser seen sketches and studies taken from the studio when he died in 1959. Thickly painted impressionistic scenes of ponies standing against a bright East Anglian sky jostle for position with smooth and shiny thoroughbreds whose jockeys are a-blaze in brightly coloured silks. 

[Explore the Art Collection >>](https://www.munningsmuseum.org.uk/collection/) 
[Read more about Castle House & Studio >>](https://www.munningsmuseum.org.uk/archive/)

## Special Exhibitions in 2027

### **22nd May to 12th September 2027** 
** 
The Art of the Newlyn School: Paintings from The Bowerman Collection**

Some of the most important paintings of the Newlyn School are coming to Dedham in the summer of 2027. Thirty-four works from the celebrated Bowerman Collection will be displayed alongside masterpieces by Sir Alfred Munnings from the museum’s own nationally important collection of his work. 

_The Art of the Newlyn School: Paintings from The Bowerman Collection_ offers a rare chance to see paintings by the artists who transformed Newlyn and West Cornwall into one of Britain’s most celebrated artistic colonies. It was amongst these artists that Alfred Munnings lived and painted in the idyllic years just before the outbreak of the First World War. 

The exhibition includes much-loved paintings by Walter Langley and rare gems by Elizabeth Forbes and Dod Procter which reveal the extraordinary range of artists who came to Cornwall from the 1880s onwards. Pictures by Stanhope Forbes, the “father of the Newlyn School”, will hang alongside those by Harold Harvey and Dame Laura Knight who, as the second generation of Newlyn artists, brought fresh colour and energy to the colony. 

Munnings Art Museum is delighted to be the only East of England venue on this major national tour by The Bowerman Collection, one of the most important private holdings of Newlyn School paintings. Founded from the private collection of David Bowerman MBE, the Bowerman Charitable Trust in Sussex was established with the aim of making great art accessible to the public. 

Paid admission to the museum in 2027 includes entry to all exhibitions

### Welcome

The Fry Public Art Gallery was opened in 1987 and houses an impressive number of paintings, prints, illustrations, wallpapers and decorative designs by artists of the 20th century and the present day who have local connections and have made a significant contribution to their field. There is an emphasis on those who for a variety of reasons settled in Great Bardfield between the early thirties of the last century and the death in 1983 of John Aldridge RA who had lived in the village for fifty years.

The Gallery is run by volunteers, both invigilators when it is open to the public and other helpers throughout the year. Please contact us if you would like to become more involved.

The Fry Art Gallery is now closed for 2026.

Thank you to everyone who has visited us this year. We look forward to welcoming you back next April with two exciting new exhibitions.

Don’t forgot our [ANNUAL SALE](https://fryartgallery.org/fry-annual-sale-this-weekend/), which this year is over the weekend of Saturday 14th and Sunday 15th November.

# We’re changing our exhibitions

While we prepare for our next season of exhibitions (opening 21 Nov), there’s still plenty to see. Explore the full historic house, including [_Pop and the Figure_](https://pallant.org.uk/whats-on/pop-and-the-figure/), discover our [new staircase installation](https://pallant.org.uk/whats-on/ro-robertson-howl/) and visit the [latest exhibition](https://pallant.org.uk/whats-on/rachel-howard-and-frank-auerbach-noise/) in our Print Room.

[Find out more](https://pallant.org.uk/exhibition-changeover/)

### Coming soon

[**Barbara Hepworth and Greece**\\ \\ Opens 21 November 2026](https://pallant.org.uk/whats-on/barbara-hepworth-and-greece/)

[**Alfred Wallis: An Artists' Artist**\\ \\ Opens 21 November 2026](https://pallant.org.uk/whats-on/alfred-wallis-an-artists-artist/)

[**Pallant Café**](https://pallant.org.uk/your-visit/eat-drink/)

#### Discover our collection

We share the story of British art from 1900 to the present. Through our world-class collection of Modern British art, made up of over 5000 artworks, we explore the contributions of British artists from new perspectives.

Discover artists such as Barbara Hepworth, Graham Sutherland, Paul Nash, Rachel Whiteread, Damien Hirst, Barbara Walker and others within different contemporary, historic, and international contexts.

[Find out more](https://pallant.org.uk/our-art/)

### Explore our Perspectives Blog

Ideas, stories, and voices from Pallant House Gallery – [dive in](https://test.pallant.org.uk/perspectives/) and see art from a new angle.

[Read the blog](https://pallant.org.uk/why-print-rachel-howard-and-frank-auerbach-noise/)

[**5 Things You Might Not Know About Barbara Hepworth**](https://pallant.org.uk/5-things-you-might-not-know-about-barbara-hepworth/)

Come and see the 'Pier Glow' as part of Stromness Glimmers – A Festival of Light. Between 6-9pm tonight and tomorrow, the street between the Pier Head and Museum will be lit up with a trail of artworks. The Pier Arts Centre’s waterfront windows will be transformed with a rich red illumination, creating a striking presence on Stromness harbour. Visible from both land and sea, the work highlights the gallery as a place of creativity, welcome and exchange, offering a subtle yet evocative beacon during the darker months. The building is best viewed from the pier opposite. Stromness Glimmers is organised by @moticollective You can visit our exhibition celebrating ten years of Móti between 10:30-5pm Tuesday-Saturday until 24th December. (Poster artwork by Mal Grieve)

On display until 24 December Moti - The First Ten Years @moticollective is a group of art and design graduates who have either studied in, returned to, or chosen to base themselves in Orkney. Their founding members were initially brought together by the Pier Arts Centre’s graduates’ exhibition Stargazing in 2015, founding the collective the following year. This exhibition, celebrating ten years since their inception, brings together the work of 17 members of Móti Collective in a wide range of media including photography, sculpture, printmaking and textiles. #PierArtsCentre #Orkneyart #MOTI

# Soane Medal 2026

_24 November 2026_

**Join us for this special event celebrating our 2026 Soane Medallist, Farshid Moussavi, at the Royal Academy of Arts.**

[Book Now](https://www.soane.org/whats-on/2026-soane-medal-lecture)

## Welcome to Sir John Soane's Museum

**Discover the extraordinary house and museum of Sir John Soane, one of the greatest English architects, who built and lived in it two centuries ago. The museum has been kept as it was at the time of his death in 1837, and displays his vast collection of antiquities, furniture, sculptures, architectural models and paintings.**

We're open Wednesday to Sunday, 10 to 5. Entry is free and you can visit by walking in on the day. Joining a highlights tour, or visiting as a group of eight or more, requires advanced booking.

[Book a group Visit](https://www.soane.org/groups) [Book a Highlights Tour](https://www.soane.org/whats-on/highlights-tour)

## Plan a visit to Sir John Soane’s spectacular Drawing Office

**Recently restored, the Drawing Office is the oldest surviving example of its kind and is now open to public tours for the first time in its 200-year history.**

This remarkable space also hosts two Artists-in-Residence each year, keeping creative practice at the heart of the Museum.

[Find out more](https://drawingoffice.soane.org/)

## Soane Late x New Architecture Writers: House Speculations

27 Nov 2026

Join New Architecture Writers and Sir John Soane’s Museum for an evening tracing Sir John’s footsteps and considering his remarkable home as a future ruin.

[FIND OUT MORE](https://www.soane.org/whats-on/soane-late-x-new-arcitechture-writers-27-nov-2026) [See All Events](https://www.soane.org/whats-on)

## Support the future of the Museum

Sir John Soane’s Museum is the smallest of the National Museums and we now welcome more visitors than ever before; free of charge, to learn, enjoy and be inspired by the story of Sir John Soane, his house and collection. Your support is vital in ensuring that this continues.

# Exhibitions & Events

Explore the latest exhibitions, events, and workshops at Rye Art Gallery. Our collection features from both emerging and established artists, as well as a stunning permanent collection. Sign up for our mailing list to stay up-to-date on upcoming events

[View Events](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/exhibitions-events)

# Explore the 
Rye Art Gallery Collection

The Permanent Collection of the Gallery comprises approximately 700 artworks, primarily two-dimensional, with a few three-dimensional pieces. Additionally, the Gallery has a collection of Archive material.

[Learn more](https://artuk.org/visit/venues/rye-art-gallery-4759)

## Artists in Focus

[Listening Piece, 2019 Limestone on hardwood base £3,000 .jpg](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/bernard-mcguigan-)

Bernard McGuigan

Bernard is a quiet modest man but full of determination and energy, which is often reflected in his work. If you take for example, 'Just the Two of Us', the movement of the piece is full of vitality, the two-figures joined not only by physical attributes but also by an emotional energy too. More recently Bernard’s work has moved towards abstraction, where marks of the artists tools are more evident, 'Autumn Days' bears this evidence where rough stone sits symmetrically next to the smooth polished stone. Another abstract piece in place at the gallery is 'Riding the Wave', which is completely smooth and polished made from limestone which depicts a large kidney form with two smaller geometric shapes inside where the subtractive process is manifest. A piece that most visitors of the gallery cannot help but stroke, the tactile nature of this artwork makes something so hard and inanimate become more lifelike offering a special kind of sensory experience.

[Towards the Sea, Emma Turpin.jpg](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/emma-turpin-)

[Emma Turpin](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/emma-turpin-)

In recent years, Emma has been exploring the notion of shelter in landscape. There are structures hidden in forests, and there are others that have almost become part of the landscape with trees bursting from inside them. Emma uses these familiar natural forms to try and find a harmonious resolution between colour and form.

[Melvn Evans _edited.jpg](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/melvyn-evans-)

Melvyn Evans

Melvyn Evans the artist, illustrator and printmaker's bold lino-cut prints and paintings, feature seascapes and landscapes. Melvyn takes inspiration from the ancient natural elements of the British landscape specifically the Hitchen Stone boundary between Yorkshire and Lancashire. A series of works including Stone Forest (2019) and Lost Land With Boat Form (2020) reimagine the fossilised ruins of a vast submerged area called Doggerland, where in around 6,500BC, rising sea levels flooded the area which originally connected Britain to continental Europe. Remnants can still be seen today at low tide in some areas particularly at Redcar beach. If there’s one thing the work of Melvyn Evans conveys it’s his love for the British countryside. In both the representation of land and the sea, through a considered use of colour and shape, his paintings and lino prints embody a historic sense of place. They explore the bonds that exist between human endeavour and the landscape as a dramatic, natural backdrop.

[Burren.jpg](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/jacqueline-stanley-arca-hrha)

Jacqueline Stanley

Stanley studied at Beckenham College of Art and Royal College of Art, London, where her teachers included Francis Bacon. A prolific painter and printmaker, her early work documented a rapidly changing London, before becoming primarily concerned with landscape. She relocated to Ireland in 1975. Teaching at the National College of Art and Design, Dublin, 1975–90. She was a director of the Black Church Print Studio and a board member of the Graphic Studio Trust. Jacqueline exhibited widely and much of her work is in major public and private collections. Among Jacqueline’s many awards include Royal College of Art Sketch club Award,1st prize in painting (1950), Young Contemporaries, 1st prize (shared with Donald Hamilton Fraser) (1950), Lord Mayor’s Exhibition, Guildhall, London, 1st Prize for Painting Lord Mayor’s Art Award (1968), Lord Mayor’s Exhibition, Guildhall, London, Print Award (1972), Taiwan International Print (Jury Award) (1987), and Awarded HRHA (2018)

[SEA TO SEA.jpg](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/keith-purser-)

Keith Purser

Keith Purser lives and works on the edge of the desert-like environment of Europe's largest shingle bank, in the shadow of Dungeness power station and within sight of the coast of France. Born in Bromley, Kent, he attended Sidcup School of Art in the 1960s.

[Mick Rooney RA Waiting and Wondering copy.jpg](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/items/mick-rooney-ra)

Mick Rooney RA

Mick Rooney studied at Sutton School of Art from 1959 to 1962, Wimbledon School of Art from 1962 to 1964, and subsequently at the Royal College of Art, London from 1964 to 1967. Here he was awarded the Austin Abbey Major Scholarship to study at the British School of Rome from 1967 to 1968, where he was commissioned by the Franciscan Order to create a wall mosaic for a new Basilica in Nazareth, Israel. Between 1968 and 1982 he taught part-time at various art colleges. Rooney’s early solo exhibitions were held from 1965 at the Fulham Gallery, London, Galerie Petit, Amsterdam, Seasons Gallery, The Hague and Patrick Seale Gallery, London, with regular solo shows being held at the Mercury Gallery, London from 1984. A retrospective of his work (covering the period 1978 to 1988) was held in 1989 and toured Folkestone, Eastbourne and Bath. Rooney’s work has been included in many group exhibitions in Britain and abroad. Among Rooney’s commissions is a painting to celebrate the centenary of the Financial Times (1988), a poster for London Underground (1990), a tapestry commissioned by TSB for Birmingham Headquarters (woven by Edinburgh Tapestry Company) and a book cover for Mr and Mrs Noah – recent poems by Brendan Kennely. Among Rooney’s many awards are ANSVAR Insurance, Towner Art Gallery, Eastbourne (1981), World of Newspapers, Daily Mirror, London (1982), Spirit of London, GLC Southbank (1983), Gulbenkian Printmakers Award (1984), John Player Portrait Award, National Portrait Gallery (1985), Daler/Rowney Prize (Royal Academy, 1986), House and Garden Magazine Award (Royal Academy, 1988), Korn/Ferry International Premier Award (Royal Academy, 1989) and First Prize, Chichester Arts Festival Exhibition. Rooney was Artist in Residence for the Towner Art Gallery, Eastbourne in 1983. He was elected Royal Academician in 1991 and in 2001 was elected to the Royal Society of Painters and Printmakers.

[See all Artists](https://www.ryeartgallery.org.uk/art-for-sale)

## Collection Spotlight

###### Black Mountain, Wales 1968 Edward Burra

Edward Burra (1905-1976) is a name that comes up regularly in Rye, as one of our most famous inhabitants there are many people who remember, recollect and eulogise about this enigmatic individual. His artwork and his life were a journey of immeasurable achievement, he was overwhelmed with illness from birth but rather than allowing this to become his identity, he worked tirelessly creating the paintings we now recognise as some of the most famous watercolours in the art world. Read more on the Curators Blog

# Welcome to Penlee House Gallery & Museum

The gallery is the perfect place to discover the art of West Cornwall, including the works of the Newlyn School and Lamorna artists. The museum covers local history, from amazing archaeological finds to fabulous ceramics, social history and fashion. After that, why not relax for a while in our brand new licensed cafe, the perfect place for morning coffee, a light lunch or afternoon tea with delicious homemade cakes. Food freshly prepared to order. 

We have a fantastic programme of regular events. Visit our [Events](https://penleehouse.org.uk/event/) page to see what’s on, to help you plan your visit.

Previous Slide Next Slide

### Home to the world’s most significant collection of William Morris’s work.

Open Tuesday to Sunday 10am to 5pm. Free entry.

[**William Morris**\\ \\ Meet William Morris, revolutionary designer, craftsman, writer, social activist, and conservationist.\\ \\ **Find out more**](https://wmgallery.org.uk/collection/about-william-morris/) [**The Collection**\\ \\ Explore the works of Morris and his contemporaries.\\ \\ **Find out more**](https://wmgallery.org.uk/collection/)

[**Deeney’s Cafe at WMG**\\ \\ Relax at Deeney’s Cafe, located on the ground floor with gorgeous sunlit views overlooking Lloyd Park.](https://www.wmgallery.org.uk/visit/cafe/)

[**Venue hire**\\ \\ The unique atmosphere of William Morris Gallery can transform any event into an unforgettable experience.](https://www.wmgallery.org.uk/visit/venue-hire/)

[**Group visits**\\ \\ The Gallery welcomes group visits and coach trips all year round.](https://www.wmgallery.org.uk/visit/group-visits/)

[**Explore the local area**\\ \\ Visit Lloyd Park, Vestry House Museum and other attractions around Waltham Forest.](https://www.wmgallery.org.uk/visit/explore-the-local-area/)

## Getting here

##### Address: 
**William Morris Gallery** 
**Lloyd Park, Forest Road** 
**London E17 4PP**

William Morris Gallery is located in Walthamstow in north-east London and is easily accessible by public transport. It’s recommended that you walk, cycle or come by public transport if possible.

[Plan your visit](https://wmgallery.org.uk/visit/)

## Accessibility

##### William Morris Gallery has an entrance with a ramp, accessible toilets and lift access to all floors.

The Gallery has been awarded the designation of ‘Dementia Friendly Venue’ by the Alzheimer’s Society. This means that it is a cultural venue in London offering a range of dementia-friendly resources.

[Find out more](https://wmgallery.org.uk/visit/access/)

## Enhance your visit

##### Find expert insights, context, and more curated content from the Gallery by viewing our guide on Bloomberg Connects, the free arts and culture app. For a seamless visitor experience, please download the Bloomberg Connects app before your visit.

[Read more & download the guide](https://www.wmgallery.org.uk/visit/bloomberg-connects-digital-guide/)

## Stanley Spencer and Gary Bunt: What a Dream

6 November — 21 March 2027

The first exhibition to bring together two artists who found beauty, humour and unexpected wonder in everyday life. It features 20 works by Gary Bunt and 15 by Spencer, including Spencer’s _Swan Upping_ (1915–19), on loan from Tate, and Bunt’s _Tribute to Stanley Spencer_ (2021), alongside final works he made for the exhibition before his death in 2025.

[Book tickets](https://stanleyspencergallery.digitickets.co.uk/event-tickets/80365?catID=68143)

[About the exhibition](https://stanleyspencer.org.uk/winter-exhibition-2026/)

### ART & PLACE

## Discover Stanley Spencer in the village that inspired him

Sir Stanley Spencer RA (1891–1959) was one of Britain’s most distinctive twentieth-century artists, known for paintings that bring everyday life together with intense imagination and spirituality.

He was born in Cookham and its streets, people and landscape became the setting for much of his work. Our collection lets you explore his life and art in the place that shaped it.

[**Stanley Spencer →**](https://stanleyspencer.org.uk/stanley-spencer-the-artist/)

A short biography

### HIS LEGACY

## Stanley Spencer's enduring influence

This profound impact on the art world, characterised by a unique blend of spirituality, realism and imagination, has left an enduring legacy that continues to captivate and inspire generations of artists and enthusiasts.

[Importance and influence](https://stanleyspencer.org.uk/importance-and-influence/)

# Cartwright Hall Art Gallery

Lister Park, Bradford, BD9 4NS

cartwright.hall@bradford.gov.uk

01274 431212

## About Cartwright Hall Art Gallery

Set within the beautiful surroundings of Lister Park, just one mile from Bradford city centre, Cartwright Hall Art Gallery has been welcoming visitors since 1904.

Home to Bradford’s nationally significant art collection, the gallery brings together Victorian, modern and contemporary art alongside changing exhibitions, family activities and events throughout the year.

Bradford was one of the first local authority museum services in the UK to actively collect work by South Asian and Black artists. Today, this nationally important collection sits alongside works from across the centuries, reflecting the city’s rich artistic and cultural heritage.

The story of Bradford’s art collection began before Cartwright Hall itself. The city’s first art museum opened on Kirkgate in 1879, where annual selling exhibitions helped establish a permanent collection for the people of Bradford. As the collection grew, Samuel Cunliffe Lister donated £40,000 towards creating a purpose-built civic art gallery within Lister Park. Cartwright Hall opened in 1904 and, more than 120 years later, continues to grow and evolve through its permanent collection and programme of changing exhibitions.

While you’re here, why not enjoy refreshments in the [Refreshment Room Café](https://bradfordmuseums.org/cartwright-hall-art-gallery/cafe/) or take time to explore [Lister Park](https://bradforddistrictparks.org/park/lister-park/), one of Bradford’s most-loved parks and home to beautiful gardens, a boating lake and family-friendly play areas.

@graph.name: Cartwright Hall Art Gallery
@graph.description:
Set within the beautiful surroundings of Lister Park, just one mile from Bradford city centre, Cartwright Hall Art Gallery has been welcoming visitors since 1904. Home to Bradford's nationally significant art collection, the gallery brings together Victorian, modern and contemporary art alongside changing exhibitions, family activities and events throughout the year. Bradford was one of the first local authority museum services in the UK to actively collect work by South Asian and Black artists. Today, this nationally important collection sits alongside works from across the centuries, reflecting the city's rich artistic and cultural heritage. The story of Bradford's art collection began before Cartwright Hall itself. The city's first art museum opened on Kirkgate in 1879, where annual selling exhibitions helped establish a permanent collection for the people of Bradford. As the collection grew, Samuel Cunliffe Lister donated £40,000 towards creating a purpose-built civic art gallery within Lister Park. Cartwright Hall opened in 1904 and, more than 120 years later, continues to grow and evolve through its permanent collection and programme of changing exhibitions. While you're here, why not enjoy refreshments in the Refreshment Room Café or take time to explore Lister Park, one of Bradford's most-loved parks and home to beautiful gardens, a boating lake and family-friendly play areas.

# Inspiring creativity. With a free entry art gallery and museum, artists’ studios, and events for everyone.

## Welcome

The Harley Foundation is an educational arts charity on the historic Welbeck estate in Nottinghamshire. Visit our **free entry gallery** **and museum** and you’ll find a world-class historic art collection, contemporary exhibitions, and family activities.

Explore our spaces further and you’ll find a community of artists, countryside art trail, and **events for everyone**.

Come on in!

## What's On

Art exhibitions, things to do with the kids, and craft workshops – find out what’s on at the Harley Foundation.

[Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/whats-on/)

## Explore

Find out more about art, history and making with our Explore pages.

[Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/explore/)

## Visit

Plan your visit to the Harley Foundation.

[Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/visit/)

## Featured

 [**Gallery**\\ \\ **The Harley Open 2026**\\ \\ 19 September 2026 — 3 January 2027\\ \\ Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/whats-on/event/the-harley-open-2026/)

 [**Museum**\\ \\ **The World’s Mine Oyster**\\ \\ Art, Nature and Collecting the Globe 20 March 2026 — 8 April 2029\\ \\ Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/whats-on/event/the-worlds-mine-oyster/)

## Learning

Enjoy learning about art at the Harley Foundation.

There are events for all ages, with workshops and talks, school trips and at-home activities.

[Find out more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/about-us/learning/)

## Studios + Artists

The Harley Foundation supports an impressive community of artists, tucked away in our idyllic studios on the historic Welbeck estate. Find out more about our studios and artists.

[Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/studios/)

## Our Community

Inspiring creativity in our local area. Find out about our projects working with schools and community groups.

[Discover more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/about/community/)

[**Reflections on Community**\\ \\ During our monthly Discover Art! session, young people worked with exhibiting artist Jennifer Vanderpool to reflect on ideas about community.\\ \\ Read more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/community/reflections-on-community/) 

[**Worksop Fun Palace**\\ \\ Every year in October, the Harley Education Team pack up their craft materials and head to Worksop Library to take part in Worksop Fun Palace.\\ \\ Read more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/community/worksop-fun-palace/) 

[**2025: Year In Review**\\ \\ Reflect on the year and see our 2025 stats\\ \\ Read more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/community/2025-in-review/) 

## Shop

Make your world more beautiful with this selection of art, handmade craft, and unique products.

[Learn more](https://harleyfoundation.org.uk/visit/dine-shop/)

# Experience Cornwall through the art, objects and artefacts that tell the story of our past.

## The Red Dress

Tickets are now on sale to see international sensation, _The Red Dress_, in January 2027.

The world’s largest collaborative embroidery project takes you on a journey around the globe, from the spectacular setting of The Heart of Cornwall Gallery. 

[Book Now](https://cornwallmuseum.digitickets.co.uk/category/76708?navItem=1366052)

Visiting us

Come and find us in the heart of Truro

Admission £10 under 18's go free

[Admission and Tickets](https://cornwallmuseum.org/visit/)

Getting Here

Situated in the city centre, just off the main high street, Cornwall Museum and Art Gallery is easy to reach.

Find out how to get here by foot, car, taxi, bus and train [here.](https://cornwallmuseum.org/visit/)

Please note Cornwall Museum and Art Gallery has no car-parking facilities.

[Find out more](https://cornwallmuseum.org/visit/#getting-here)

Accessibility

We are committed to being a museum for everyone. The museum is fully wheelchair accessible, with unisex accessible toilets, ramp and lift, baby changing facilities, shop and cafe. Sensory maps are available from the reception area.

For more information and guides around accessibility are available at the museum. The guide is intended to give you a pre-visit overview of the facilities we provide. Please contact us if you need further advice, information or have specific requirements ahead of your visit.

Quieter hours: If you are planning a visit and would prefer a more relaxed experience, our quieter hours tend to be between 2 – 4pm during school term times. Sunny days are usually quiet and rainy days are usually busier.

[Find out more](https://cornwallmuseum.org/visit/#accessibility)

## What's on

[**The Red Dress**\\ \\ \\ \\   **5 - 30 January, 2027**\\ \\ 380 embroiderers from 51 countries contributed to the world's largest collaborative embroidery project, telling stories through stitch from across the...](https://cornwallmuseum.org/exhibition/the-red-dress/)

[**Art Any Way**\\ \\ \\ \\   **14 September, 2026 - 30 January, 2027**\\ \\ Works by artists compelled to create, offering fresh and exhilarating perspectives along the way.](https://cornwallmuseum.org/exhibition/art-any-way/)

[**Fired Moon**\\ \\ \\ \\   **21 September - 23 November, 2026**\\ \\ Ceramicist Chris Prindl puts a uniquely Cornish take on the Korean Moon Jar - one of the most celebrated forms in ceramic history.](https://cornwallmuseum.org/exhibition/fired-moon/)

[**Winter is Coming…**\\ \\ \\ \\   **28 September, 2026 - 16 January, 2027**\\ \\ Dive into a new season with atmospheric modernist works from Cornwall's School's Art Collection.](https://cornwallmuseum.org/exhibition/winter-is-coming/)
