# WELCOME

The Stained Glass Museum is the only museum dedicated to the art of stained glass in the UK. The museum boasts a nationally-designated collection of stained glass, associated designs, materials and tools which reveal the development of this unique art from the 13th century to present day. 

The museum’s permanent gallery space is located in the triforium of Ely Cathedral. It houses a chronological display featuring stained glass from the museum’s own collection as well as from partner organisations the V&A and the Royal Collection. Displayed at eye-level, visitors can experience this art form at close quarters. 

An engaging learning programme for all ages sees practical glass workshops led by professional artists, talks, tours and family activities held throughout the year. 

[SGM gallery - general shot](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/lluniau/sgmgallery2.jpg 'SGM gallery - general shot')

# BOOK TICKETS

**Visitors wishing to visit only the Stained Glass Museum** can purchase tickets on arrival or [book online in advance here](https://www.elycathedral.org/events/stained-glass-museum) 

**Visitors wishing to visit the Stained Glass Museum and Ely Cathedral** can purchase a joint ticket online in advance from Ely Cathedral here: [Book a joint Cathedral + Stained Glass Museum ticket (Joint Tickets)](https://www.elycathedral.org/events/visitor-tickets). _After selecting an Ely Cathedral Visitor Ticket (adult or child), you will be offered the option to add a Stained Glass Museum ticket at a combined ticket price._ 

### Opening Hours

**Winter** (1 November – 31 March) 
Monday - Saturday 
10:00am – 4:00pm (last admission 3:30pm) 

**Summer** (1 April – 31 October) 
Monday - Saturday 
10:00am – 5:00pm (last admission 4:30pm) 

**Upcoming Closures** 
EARLY CLOSURE: Thursday 10th December 2026 from 2pm 
CLOSED: Friday 25th December 2026 
CLOSED: Saturday 26th December 2026 
CLOSED: Monday 28th December 2026 

_Please check here for scheduled closures. The Museum is located in a working Cathedral building, and occasionally has to close for special events and services. Please visit [Ely Cathedral's website](https://www.elycathedral.org/plan-your-visit/information-for-visitors/opening-times)_ _for any changes in access to the main Cathedral building._ 

### Admission

_Our annual passes are valid for 12 months from the date of your first booking and mean you can come back and visit the museum as many times as often as you'd like for a full year. Please [Gift Aid](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/gift-aid.php)_ _your admission if you are able to do so._ 

**Adults:** £6.50 
**Students:** £6:00 
**Under 16s:** Free (when accompanied by a paying adult) 

**Free entry** to The Stained Glass Museum for National Art Pass holders, Museum Association members, Friends of Ely Cathedral, Friends of The Stained Glass Museum. _Please show your relevant membership card to gain free entry_ 

**[The Ely Passport](https://www.visitely.org.uk/the-ely-passport/)** is a joint ticket giving access to four of Ely's fantastic heritage destinations including the museum, the Cathedral, and nearby Oliver Cromwell's House and Ely Museum. Available to purchase from each participating venue or online from [Visit Ely](https://www.visitely.org.uk/the-ely-passport/) 

### Location and Access

The Stained Glass Museum is on an upper level of a Grade-I listed medieval Cathedral and entrance is via a spiral staircase (40 steps). For more information see our [access](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/access.php) page. 
What 3 Words address ///spines.cupboards.removals 

**By Train:** Ely is 1 hour 15 minutes by rail from London, and 15-20 minutes from Cambridge. The Stained Glass Museum is a 15 minute walk from Ely rail station. There is a taxi rank outside the station. 

**By Car:** Ely is situated on the A10 north of Cambridge. There is a large free car park within 300 yards of the Cathedral. [Parking in Ely](https://eastcambs.gov.uk/sites/default/files/2024-10/Ely%20car%20park%20map.pdf) 

### Preparing for your Visit

**[Group Visits](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/groups.php)**[:](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/groups.php) If you are planning to visit as part of a group please contact us. Discounted entry is available for groups of 10+. [Group Visits Information](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/uploads/sgm%20group%20visit%20information%20(2020).pdf) 

**[School Visits](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/schools.php)**[:](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/schools.php) We welcome visits from schools, colleges and other educational groups. Please contact our Learning Officers learning@stainedglassmuseum.com or telephone 01353 660347 

### Facilities

**Bags:** The museum does not permit large bags in the museum gallery, in order to protect its collections. 

**Activities for children:** The museum is very family-friendly and there are a number of activities for children. [Family visitors](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/families.php) 

**Dogs:**We are a dog-friendly museum. Well-behaved dogs are permitted in the museum, when accompanied by their responsible owners! 

**Photography:** Photography is permitted in the main gallery for personal use only, providing that you adhere to the stipulations outlined in our [Photography Policy](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/uploads/sgm%20photography%20policy%20(april%2019).pdf). 

**Shop:** The Museum has a well-stocked [gift shop](https://the-stained-glass-museum.myshopify.com/) with exclusive handmade glass gifts and books dedicated to the history of stained glass. Our shop is open to everyone and you do not have to have a ticket to the museum to browse our shop. 

**Toilets:** Please note that there are no toilet facilities within the museum itself. However, visitors with a Cathedral tickets can use the toilet facilities available on the ground floor of Ely Cathedral, or there nearby public toilets on Palace Green (all within 5 minutes walking distance). 

**Cafes:** The Museum does not have a cafe although there are many cafes and restaurants in Ely including The Almonry within the grounds of Ely Cathedral. There are also a number of cafes in the city centre just a short 5-10 minute walk away. 

**Researchers:** [Search the Museum's collections](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/collections.php) and [reference library](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/librarysearch.php) online. Objects in the library and reserve collection can be visited via prior appointment. Please make an appointment with the Curator. 

### Find Out More

Please see our [Visiting FAQ](https://stainedglassmuseum.com/visitingfaq.php) page to find out more about your visit.

###### Charmaine Watkiss, _The warrior’s presence is safeguarded for generations to come_ , 2024, water soluble graphite, pencil, watercolour, coloured pencil and ink on paper. © _2026 Charmaine Watkiss. All rights reserved, DACS._

# Charmaine Watkiss

### The things we hold sacred

#### Until 11 April 2027

##### **Floor 3**

A major new solo exhibition of drawings and sculpture by British artist Charmaine Watkiss. Alongside major loans from private and museum collections, the exhibition includes newly commissioned sculptures and the artist’s most significant sculptural installation to date.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/charmaine-watkiss-the-things-we-hold-sacred/)

###### Claire Buckerfield & Black Country Type, Logo (2026), Digital drawing

# Vibration Calibration

### Black Country Type & Claire Buckerfield

#### Until 28 February 2027

Taking its name from a mechanical process that measures the accuracy of vibration sensors, the exhibition offers a recalibration of our perceptions of the Black Country through the artists’ portrayal of the area.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/vibration-calibration-black-country-type-claire-buckerfield/)

###### Laura Onions, Gaping #5, 2025, Monotype on newsprint. Courtesy the artist.

# Laura Onions

#### Until 6 December 2026

##### **Artists’ Studio, Floor 1**

Laura will use her residency to explore the processes of contact, transference and pressure within her printmaking practice and how these physical actions might correspond to personal, social and environmental landscapes, including the burgeoning pressure of the climate emergency.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/laura-onions/)

###### The two Mothers photographed inside The New Art Gallery Walsall, July 2025. Photo: Carl Gibbons

# Tereza Bušková

### Mothers without Hands

#### Until 15 November 2026

##### **Community Gallery, Ground Floor**

**Curated by Dr. Nicola Baird**

The exhibition takes its title from _The Girl Without Hands_, a 1200-year-old fairy tale collected and revised by the Brothers Grimm. Featuring a girl whose hands are cut off and magically restored, it is a story not only about patriarchal oppression, persecution, violation and trauma, but also survival, strength and healing.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/tereza-buskova-mothers-without-hands/)

# The Garman Ryan Collection

### Permanent Collection

This prestigious collection was donated to the people of Walsall in 1973 by Kathleen Garman. Kathleen had grown up in Wednesbury, lived her adult life in London, but wanted to give something back to her home county, believing it was important for culture to exist outside of the capital.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/collections-library/)

###### Andrew Tift, Portrait of Kitty (Transition), 2006, acrylic on board. Permanent Collection, The New Art Gallery Walsall.

# Face Value

### Contemporary Portraits from the Collections

#### Until 23 May 2027

Inspired by the strong focus on portraits in the Garman Ryan Collection, this temporary exhibition brings together a selection of artworks from the Gallery’s Permanent Collection.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/face-value-contemporary-portraits-from-the-collections/)

# Diwali Community Day

#### Saturday 14 November 2026

11am-3pm

Join us for our annual celebration of the Festival of Lights.

Free, drop-in. All welcome.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/event/diwali-community-day-2/)

# Sunday Art Club

12-3pm, Ages 4+

Free, drop-in

Our weekly art club for children and young people. Meet artists and creatives and learn to paint, print, sculpt, craft and more!

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/event/newspaper-and-raffia-cats/)

# Charmaine Watkiss

### The things we hold sacred

#### Until 11 April 2027

##### **Floor 3**

A major new solo exhibition of drawings and sculpture by British artist Charmaine Watkiss. Alongside major loans from private and museum collections, the exhibition includes newly commissioned sculptures and the artist’s most significant sculptural installation to date.

[**Read more**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/exhibition/charmaine-watkiss-the-things-we-hold-sacred/)

## Welcome

Our aim is to increase the understanding and enjoyment of arts and culture through our dynamic exhibition, education and events programme.

[**Walsall for All Pledge**](https://thenewartgallerywalsall.org.uk/2020/09/07/walsall-for-all-pledge/)

We declare our support for a more integrated Walsall; to do what we can to help make Walsall fairer for everyone and to connect with other people and organisations that share our goals.

## Gallery Shop

Find inspiration in our shop with a curated selection of books, art materials, greeting cards, jewellery, stationery, and exclusive limited edition prints.

- [Pause the carousel](https://www.warwickdc.gov.uk/)

The Grade II listed Royal Pump Rooms is owned and managed by Warwick District Council’ Arts Section. Opened in 1814, it was the grandest of Leamington’s spa buildings and remained in operation providing swimming and water treatments until the 1990s, when it was converted into a cultural facility for the town. [Find out more about it's history](https://www.warwickdc.gov.uk/royalpumprooms/info/29/history). 

**This popular cultural and tourist attraction is home to the [Visitor Information Centre and Box Office](https://www.warwickdc.gov.uk/royalpumprooms/info/57/visitor_information_centre), [Leamington Spa Art Gallery & Museum](https://www.warwickdc.gov.uk/royalpumprooms/info/2/leamington_spa_art_gallery_and_museum), [Leamington Library](https://library.warwickshire.gov.uk/-/leamington-spa-library-information-centre), [the Larder café](https://g.co/kgs/MQbV2sQ), and various [hireable event spaces](https://www.warwickdc.gov.uk/royalpumprooms/info/44/room_hire).**

[**The Larder**\\ \\ Enjoy homemade meals, great coffee, and local cakes. Link opens TripAdvisor page.](https://www.tripadvisor.co.uk/Restaurant_Review-g187063-d17714595-Reviews-The_Royal_Pump_Rooms_Cafe_Bar-Leamington_Spa_Warwickshire_England.html)

## Public Notice

## Grant Museum of Zoology

The Grant Museum is home to 100,000 specimens from every continent, every ocean, and every animal group. The collection has been used in teaching and research since 1828.

[Navigate to Petrie Museum of Egyptian and Sudanese Archaeology](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/museums-collections/petrie-museum-egyptian-and-sudanese-archaeology)

## Petrie Museum of Egyptian and Sudanese Archaeology

The Petrie Museum is home to one of the world's largest and most important collections of Egyptian and Sudanese archaeology, telling the stories of people who lived in the Nile Valley in the past.

[Navigate to UCL Art Museum](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/museums-collections/ucl-art-museum)

## UCL Art Museum

UCL Art Museum holds over 10,000 sculptures, paintings, prints and drawings from the 1490s to today. Explore some of the collection through displays in our Prints & Drawings Room.

## Explore our collections

[Pathology Museum](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/museums-collections/ucl-pathology-museum)

## Pathology Museum

The pathology collection at UCL contains 8,000 human pathology specimens used for teaching, research and public engagement in human health.

[Science Collections](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/museums-collections/ucl-science-collections)

## Science Collections

The Science Collections contain objects related to UCL's research and scientific advancement and are used to critically reflect on our collective past.

[Special Collections](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/library/special-collections)

## Special Collections

UCL Special Collections is an outstanding collection of over 10,000 metres of rare books, archives and manuscripts, dating from the 4th century to the present day.

[Auto-icon of Jeremy Bentham](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/museums-collections/auto-icon-jeremy-bentham)

## Auto-icon of Jeremy Bentham

Jeremy Bentham's Auto-icon, or self-image, consists of Bentham's preserved skeleton, dressed in his own clothes, and surmounted by a wax head.

[Anthropology Collections](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/social-historical-sciences/anthropology/about-us/biological-anthropology-collection)

## Anthropology Collections

UCL Anthropology's collections of biological anthropology and ethnography.

[Archaeology Collections](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/social-historical-sciences/archaeology/research/our-facilities-and-archaeology-collections)

## Archaeology Collections

UCL Institute of Archaeology's collections of archaeological material.

[Geology Collections](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/mathematical-physical-sciences/earth-sciences/facilities-and-infrastructure/rock-room)

## Geology Collections

UCL Earth Sciences' collection of rocks, minerals and fossils.

## Research and teaching with our collections

[Research Institute for Collections](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/research-institute-collections)

## Research Institute for Collections

A virtual centre for research, teaching and public engagement inspired by and using UCL’s collections.

[Object Based Learning Laboratory](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/museums-collections/working-our-collections/object-based-learning-laboratory)

## Object Based Learning Laboratory

A space for teaching through hands-on learning with UCL collections and archives.

## Latest news

[Rare Grant Museum specimens featured at London premiere of new environmental film](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/news/2026/jul/rare-grant-museum-specimens-featured-london-premiere-new-environmental-film)

### Rare Grant Museum specimens featured at London premiere of new environmental film

Specimens from the Grant Museum of Zoology were showcased on the green carpet for the premiere of 'How to Live on Earth', a new documentary exploring humanity's relationship with the natural world.

23 Jul 2026

[Petrie Museum curator Anna Garnett awarded for Celebrating Education](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/news/2026/jun/petrie-museum-curator-anna-garnett-awarded-celebrating-education)

### Petrie Museum curator Anna Garnett awarded for Celebrating Education

Anna Garnett, curator of the Petrie Museum of Egyptian and Sudanese Archaeology, has been recognised for her work with a win in the Celebrating Education category of the UCL Education Awards.

19 Jun 2026

[Former Petrie curator celebrated in Faces of UCL campaign](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/engage/news/2026/mar/former-petrie-curator-celebrated-faces-ucl-campaign)

### Former Petrie curator celebrated in Faces of UCL campaign

Barbara Adams, former curator of the Petrie Museum, features as one of 200 Faces of UCL as part of the university’s bicentenary celebrations.

27 Mar 2026

If you have any questions related to our museums, please contact our team. Our phone line is open 10am to 5pm, Tuesday to Saturday.

Our vision

UCL President & Provost, Dr Michael Spence, writes about the need for universities to engage with their local communities and to serve society locally and nationally while listening to diverse views.

Welcome to the UCL events calendar - talks, seminars, workshops, lectures, performances and exhibitions are open to everyone. There are in-person and virtual events available. Book your place today!

In 1826, UCL was founded as London’s very first university. On 11th February this year, we marked our 200th anniversary and the beginning of a year of celebration. Join in our events and activities!

### Upcoming Events

## Christmas Market

Join us for a festive Christmas Market at Jupiter Artland, filled with independent artists, delicious food and seasonal magic!

[Find out more](https://www.jupiterartland.org/christmas-market/)

## M.I.A.S.M.A Programme

Designed to hold the manifestations of this season: grief and love, loss and memory.

[Find out more](https://www.jupiterartland.org/m-i-a-s-m-a-public-programme/)

# Our collection

[View all](https://www.jupiterartland.org/all-art/collection/ 'View all')

- [- Laura Aldridge\\ \\ **A Cosmic Reset**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/laura-aldridge-a-cosmic-reset/ 'A Cosmic Reset')

- [- Florence Peake\\ \\ **To Love and To Cherish**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/to-love-and-to-cherish/ 'To Love and To Cherish')

- [- Tracey Emin\\ \\ **I Lay Here For You**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/tracey-emin/ 'I Lay Here For You')

- [- Rachel Maclean\\ \\ **upside mimi ᴉɯᴉɯ uʍop**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/rachel-maclean/ 'upside mimi ᴉɯᴉɯ uʍop')

- [- Ian Hamilton Finlay\\ \\ **Temple Of Apollo**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/ian-hamilton-finlay-temple-of-apollo/ 'Temple Of Apollo')

- [- Marc Quinn\\ \\ **Love Bomb**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/marc-quinn-love-bomb/ 'Love Bomb')

- [- Shane Waltener\\ \\ **Over Here**](https://www.jupiterartland.org/art/shane-waltener-over-here/ 'Over Here')

### More at Jupiter Artland

## Landscape

At the heart of this developing landscape is the inexplicable force that connects the unconscious speech of the landscape with the literate vision of artists. This powerful pull has inspired artists to notice small things that the casual viewer may not, but often great work is based upon the study of maps, research of papers, stories, anecdotes – the ephemeral legends that make Jupiter such a rich and vital place – but, most importantly, from listening to the landscape.

[Learn more about landscape](https://www.jupiterartland.org/landscape/)

## Learning

Beyond its status as ‘museum’ or ‘gallery’, Jupiter seeks to be a more vital institution, one in which education and outreach is at the heart of its ethos; our belief is that art, and its transformative power, is for everyone, and our aim is to engage with every single child in Scotland, by offering free school visits throughout the year.

[Find out more](https://www.jupiterartland.org/learning/learning-foundation/)

## Shop

Whether you’re seeking a book to awaken your inner artist or a meaningful gift for someone special, you’ll find something that sparks joy and imagination. Come for the art, discover the magic – and take home a piece that speaks to your soul.

## Eat

Join us at our wonderfully designed ‘Café Party’ and immerse yourself within the trompe l’oeil of Nicolas Party’s expansive mural, or grab a bite at the Silverstreak Takeaway or at the Kiosk!

## [Become a Member](https://www.jupiterartland.org/memberships/)

### A Barograph? Maybe not...

Collections Assistant Sean Taylor examines a Mid-Century cased device and discovers a box of surprises.

Hit the link below to read the full article on Sunderland Heritage Partnership website.

Find out more

### Harmful or Helpful: Victorian Medicines

Collections Assistant Rebecca Stonehouse examines vials, tins and apothecary draws to reveal the characteristics, uses and dangers of Victorian and Edwardian-era medicines.

Hit the link below to read the full article on Sunderland Heritage Partnership website.

Find out more

[Find out more](https://sunderlandheritage.org/projects/object-of-the-month-the-roman-antefix)

### Brennius Hortius Caeser presents The Roman Antefix

Collections Assistant Tony Drake (aka Brennius Hortius Caeser) looks at a Roman antefix – a type of decorative roof tile.

Hit the link below to watch the video and read the full article on Sunderland Heritage Partnership website.

Find out more

# A quiet retreat for England's great landscape painter.

 [House image](https://turnershouse.org/the-house/) [**The House**](https://turnershouse.org/the-house/)

In 1813, England's great landscape painter J.M.W. Turner built a small villa, Sandycombe Lodge, on a large plot near the Thames at Twickenham.

[Learn More](https://turnershouse.org/the-house/) 

 [Events image](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/) [**Events & Exhibitions**](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/)

Turner's House hosts exhibitions on Turner's art and legacy, with talks, creative workshops, family activities, member and community events.

[See What's On](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/) 

 [History image](https://turnershouse.org/the-house/history/) [**The History**](https://turnershouse.org/the-house/history/)

Sandycombe Lodge was built by 1813 to the designs of J.M.W. Turner; to provide a quiet retreat for him and his elderly father.

[Discover More](https://turnershouse.org/the-house/history/) 

---

## Discover what's on

Turner's House hosts exhibitions on Turner's art and legacy, with talks, creative workshops, family activities, member events, and community gatherings.

[See what's on](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events) 

[Event image](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/upcycled-fabric-wreaths-festive-fizz/)

Christmas, Classes & Workshops[**Upcycled Fabric Wreaths & Festive Fizz**](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/upcycled-fabric-wreaths-festive-fizz/) [25 November 2026](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/upcycled-fabric-wreaths-festive-fizz/)

Join us for a festive evening creating your own unique fabric wreath using patterned fabrics and upcycled materials. Entry includes patterned and printed fabrics and ribbons, a metal floristry hoop base, 2 glasses of fizz and nibbles, with festive music and chatter in Turner’s own sitting room. Accessible to all- and non alcoholic alternatives available. [… Upcycled Fabric Wreaths & Festive Fizz](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/upcycled-fabric-wreaths-festive-fizz/)

[Book a ticket](https://turnershouse.beaconforms.com/form/990336f7) [Learn more](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/upcycled-fabric-wreaths-festive-fizz/) 

[Event image](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shopping-at-turners-house/)

Christmas[**Christmas Open House & Shopping at Turner’s House**](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shopping-at-turners-house/) [6 December 2026](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shopping-at-turners-house/)

Join us at Turner’s House for a pop up Christmas mini market; local makers and artisans, artists and products, with a mulled cider and a mince pie! Sunday 6th December 11am-4pm. If you are interested in being part of the pop up fair, we have 8 spaces available for a donation of £ 55/each to [… Christmas Open House & Shopping at Turner’s House](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shopping-at-turners-house/)

[Learn more](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shopping-at-turners-house/) 

[Event image](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shop-open-days/)

Christmas[**Christmas Shop Open Days**](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shop-open-days/) [19 November 2026 - 17 December 2026](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shop-open-days/)

Come on to shop perfect gifts for art lovers!

[Learn more](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/christmas-shop-open-days/) 

[Event image](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/sip-paint-christmas-cards/)

Christmas, Classes & Workshops[**Sip & Paint, Christmas Cards**](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/sip-paint-christmas-cards/) [2 December 2026](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/sip-paint-christmas-cards/)

Join us for a relaxed winter evening creating your own personalised Christmas cards. Decorate them with beautiful gold and silver motifs, ready to send to the special people in your life.

Your ticket includes a two-hour creative session, two glasses of fizz (non alcoholic also available), and all the materials you’ll need.

Create something personal and make a lasting impression on your loved ones this Christmas.

[Book a ticket](https://turnershouse.beaconforms.com/form/e89059b7) [Learn more](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/sip-paint-christmas-cards/)

A focused workshop inspired by a painting by Turner or an artist connected to him. The session begins with an illustrated introduction, followed by a practical art workshop. Inspired by John Ruskin’s silhouette of Turner, this session explores the popular art of silhouette-making. Your ticket all the materials you’ll need.

[Book a ticket](https://turnershouse.beaconforms.com/form/2968aff1) [Learn more](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/studio-sessions-exploring-turner-7/)

[Book a ticket](https://turnershouse.beaconforms.com/form/ad9d1e45) [Learn more](https://turnershouse.org/whats-on/events/a-georgian-christmas-friday-late/) 

## Support Turner's House

## Support 
Turner's House

 [**Make a donation**](https://turnershouse.org/support-us/donate/)

We rely entirely on admissions, grants and donations to support running costs, education and exhibitions.

[Donate Now](https://turnershouse.org/support-us/donate/) 

 [**Memberships**](https://turnershouse.org/support-us/membership/)

J.M.W. Turner could not have flourished without the support of generous individuals being patrons of the arts.

[Get a membership](https://turnershouse.org/support-us/membership/) 

 [**Volunteer with us**](https://turnershouse.org/get-involved/volunteer-roles/)

The Friends continue to support the aims of Sandycombe Lodge to continue being a small museum and learning centre.

[Volunteer](https://turnershouse.org/get-involved/volunteer-roles/) 

 [**Leave a Legacy**](https://turnershouse.org/support-us/leave-a-legacy/)

Thinking of leaving money to a good cause? Leaving a legacy in your Will is a great way to support this charity.

[Learn More](https://turnershouse.org/support-us/leave-a-legacy/) 

## Celebrate Turner's 250th birthday at the place he found inspiration

There's no better time to visit Turner's House than in the year of his 250th birthday. Discover the quiet, domestic space that Turner used as his retreat from the London art world.

[Learn More](https://turnershouse.org/visit-us/plan-your-visit/) 

---

"Turner's House is a hidden gem and a must-visit for art and history lovers! The house is beautifully preserved, giving an intimate glimpse into the life and work of J.M.W. Turner."

– Turner's House Visitor

## Who was J.M.W Turner?

In 1807 J.M.W. Turner, then a young but already well-known and commercially successful painter, bought two plots of land on the edges of two large estates between Twickenham and Richmond Bridge.

[Book a ticket](https://turnershouse.tygit.com/shop/group-calendar/pk/d4178a3717ae503fdcdb5c965bedbff1/groupId/2404) 

## A window into the great artist's mind.

Turner used this peaceful spot, with no other buildings nearby, to retreat from the pressures of the London art world, to walk and sketch along the Thames, to fish with one or two close companions, and occasionally to entertain larger groups of friends.

[Book a ticket](https://turnershouse.tygit.com/shop/group-calendar/pk/d4178a3717ae503fdcdb5c965bedbff1/groupId/2404) 

## Get Involved at Turner's House

Be part of the incredible team that brings J.M.W. Turner's house and garden to life, and engage with art and local history.

[Become a volunteer](https://turnershouse.org/get-involved/volunteer-roles/) 

## How to find us

Turner's House is located at Sandycombe Lodge, 40 Sandycoombe Road, St Margarets, Twickenham TW1 2LR. 
We are easily accessible by train, bus or on foot.

[Plan your visit](https://turnershouse.org/visit-us/plan-your-visit) 

## Subscribe to our newsletter

Be first to hear about new exhibitions, events and talks.

## **A home for art, ideas and the Scul?tures of George Wyllie**

# **About the Wyllieum**

**In keeping with Wyllie’s own approach to his work, The Wyllieum is a free, welcoming space of inspiration and invention, posing questions around what art is and can be.**

**Home to the largest collection of works by George Wyllie in the world, The Wyllieum, which sits on the River Clyde in Greenock, showcases Wyllie’s work and legacy, will host a rolling display of exhibitions and displays of art which connect to Wyllie by outlook or ethos alongside a permanent collection display showing items from the George Wyllie Estate, ephemera and archival material. The year-round gallery programme showcases Wyllie’s practice and places it in dialogue with his collaborators while also creating a platform for contemporary artistic responses to his work.**

Entry is free although [**donations**](https://www.wyllieum.com/support) are gratefully accepted.

**See** [**Gallery One**](https://www.wyllieum.com/exhibitions) **page for more information.**

# **George Wyllie (1921-2012)**

**Born in Glasgow in 1921, George Wyllie trained as an engineer with the Post Office before serving in the Royal Navy from 1942 to 1946. He was a Customs and Excise Officer for thirty years before becoming a full-time artist in his late fifties, pioneering socially engaged artwork such as the _Straw Locomotive_ (1987), which hung over an empty Clyde as a requiem for Glasgow's engineering prowess; and the _Paper Boat_ (1989), a reminder that over two fifths of the world's merchant ships were launched in The Clyde in the early 1900s.**

**Many of George’s major works have become more prescient over time. The aforementioned _Straw Locomotive_ and _Paper Boat_ communicated the hole left in communities after industry was ripped from them in the 1980s. He also built sculptures that depict a home buckling under the pressure of its over burdened mortgage, and his play _A Day Down A Goldmine_ \- performed at Glasgow’s Third Eye Centre and Tramway, The Whitworth, and the ICA and starring alongside George at various times, Russell Hunter, Bill Paterson and John Bett. ADDAG chronicled the origins of the modern banking system and its inherent inequalities.**

**George’s sense of social justice and equality was formed, in no small part, by his experiences as a younger man and were compounded by Wyllie’s experiences during the Second World War; serving in the Royal Navy George was one of the first foreign nationals to visit Hiroshima shortly after America dropped the atomic bomb.**

**By the late 1970s George had retired as a customs and excise worker in order to focus entirely on art. A friendship with gallerist Ricky Demarco led to horizon expanding meetings with other artists and creative figures including Joseph Beuys and George Rickey whose influence can be clearly seen in a range of Wyllie’s later works, including his series of outdoor _Equilibrium Spires_: wire sculptures which he placed in various locations, ranging from the remote Gruinard Island in the Inner Hebrides to the Berlin Reichstag.**

**It was during this time that George met Barbara Grigor, the chair of The Scottish Sculpture Trust, and her husband filmmaker Murray Grigor - who went on to make the influential film _The Wh?sman_ about Wyllie and his work. Their ongoing influence and support was hugely important for George as his career as an artist progressed: Find out more at** [**Georgewyllie.com**](https://georgewyllie.com)

**2026 is a landmark year for The Wyllieum as we team up with the Royal Scottish Academy to mark their bi-centenary celebrations. George Wyllie was an Academician and enjoyed the friendship of many other artists who were similarly honoured. With this in mind we have developed a series of very special exhibitions which link the RSA, George Wyllie and the ever-inspiring Clyde.**

## **What’s On**

### **21 February - 31 May 2026**

### **George Wyllie RSA (1921-2012)**** 
From the Clyde to Sarajavo 
to the Venice Lagoon**

An exhibition curated by RSA Past President Arthur Watson

This exhibition marks the 200th Anniversary of The Royal Scottish Academy (RSA) and shows how George Wyllie was embraced by Scotlands pre-eminent arts institution, and backed by some of Scotland’s most eminent sculptors. It was through Richard Demarco HRSA that Wyllie met Joseph Beuys, working with him in Scotland and Germany. He was also invited to the USA to make work in the studio of sculptor George Rickey. 

Work is included in this exhibition by four of George’s co-exhibitors at the first Scottish sculpture open exhibition, Kildrummy castle, Aberdeenshire and at Richard Demarco’s _New Scottish Art_ exhibition in Sarajevo. Large works by current Academicians Edward Summerton RSA and Arthur Watson PPRSA bring scale to the exhibition and documentation by Richard Demarco HRSA and Andy Dewar adds context.

The exhibition includes work by Benno Schotz RSA, Frank Pottinger RSA, Andrew Stenhouse RSA, Gareth Fisher PRSA, Jake Harvey RSA, Fred Bushe RSA and George Wyllie RSA, on loan from the RSA Collections.

[www.royalscottishacademy.org](https://www.royalscottishacademy.org/partners/21/)

Image: Garth Ivan

### **27 June - 31 October 2026**

### **Claire Barclay RSA**** 
B.e.i.n.g. B.u.o.y.a.n.t.**

Claire Barclay RSA is the first artist commissioned to make work in response to the context of the Wyllieum to be exhibited within the impressive main gallery space. She will bring together a number of conceptual strands, including revisiting the work of artist Joseph Beuys who George befriended in the 1980s.

The work of all three artists share an obsessive interest in exploration, combining materials and objects in provocative and often absurd ways in order to draw attention to their wider imbedded cultural roles and meanings.

Both Claire and George Wyllie share a strong connection to the Clyde and experiences that instil respect for the uncontrollable and changeable nature of the sea and prompt thinking about how we deal with patterns and unpredictability within our lives. A sense of switching of perspective from land to sea will be echoed within the work through spatial interventions and the use of the panoramic windows of the gallery space where looking out and looking in will have equal consideration. The title may also suggest that rise and fall of individual and societal optimism can provide potential for change and opportunity.

[www.clairebarclay.net](https://www.clairebarclay.net/)

Image: Garth Ivan

supported by

[Henry Moore Foundation logo](https://henry-moore.org/)

### **14 November - 29 March 2027**

### **Georgina Porteous** **_Flax Seeds Grow as the Cosmic Humblebum Goes Majestic_**

Georgina’s practice explores sculpture, place, material and imagination, often working with scale, humour and unexpected transformations.

For this exhibition she will present a new sculptural work developed through ongoing research with the Wyllieum, responding to George Wyllie’s playful, questioning approach to art, and his belief in the power of imagination, curiosity and the unexpected. 

_Flax seeds grow as the cosmic humblebum goes majestic_ is an invitation to look, wonder and perhaps question what you think you are seeing.

The work plays with scale, absurdity and transformation, bringing together the playful and the monumental to create something that is both familiar and completely unexpected.

Georgina is an alumni of RSA new contemporaries having been featured in the annual exhibition 2009 following her graduation from Moray School of Art.

[GeorginaPorteous.com](https://georginaporteous.com/)

# Royal Albert Memorial Museum Exeter

## Welcome to RAMM

## Getting here

Royal Albert Memorial 
Museum & Art Gallery 
Queen St, Exeter, EX4 3RX

### By foot

Our location in Queen Street is well signposted from Exeter Quay, Cathedral Green, and the city’s main shopping areas.

### Bike

Bicycle parking can be found to the rear of the museum, outside Exeter Phoenix.

### Bus and coach

Most city buses stop in the High Street or Queen Street. The main bus station is on Paris Street, and the nearest drop-off point for coaches is in Queen Street outside Central station. Local bus routes and timetables are available through Stagecoach.

### Train

Exeter Central Station is 100 metres away. Leave the station through its Queen Street entrance and turn left to reach us. St David’s Station is a 15 minute walk or short bus or taxi ride away.

### Car

The Guildhall Shopping Centre and Mary Arches car parks are nearby. Please note Queen Street is now one-way. Exeter’s Park and Ride bus services stop in Paris Street or South Street. 
We have two parking spaces for blue badge holders at our Garden Entrance. These spaces can only be used by permit holders. Please call 01392 265960 during opening hours to book your free temporary permit.

# The Women’s Art Collection

The Women's Art Collection, at Murray Edwards College, University of Cambridge, is Europe's largest publicly accessible collection of modern and contemporary art by women. The Collection, praised by the Guardian as 'world class', is open daily from 10am-6pm. Entry is free.

## What Remains

Through contemporary artists, What Remains celebrates 40 years since The Women's Art Collection acquired its first artwork.

[Find out more](https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/womens-art-collection/exhibition/what-remains)﻿

# Young Gallery

###### Edwin Young painting ©Young & Creasey Gallery Trust

**Your free art museum in the centre of Salisbury.**

Free admission to all exhibitions. Located upstairs in Salisbury Library.

## Current exhibitions

## [Gallery 1 - Permanent collection](https://www.younggallerysalisbury.org.uk/article/9461/Gallery-1-Permanent-collection)

Visit Gallery 1 to see artworks from the Young Gallery's collection of over 4000 objects.

## [Gallery 2 - Drawing Together](https://www.younggallerysalisbury.org.uk/article/9455/Gallery-2-Drawing-Together)

From 11 September see the Drawing Together: The Bath Academy of Art at Corsham exhibition in Gallery 2.

## [Gallery 3 - Supporters of the Young Gallery Members' Show](https://www.younggallerysalisbury.org.uk/article/9459/Gallery-3-Supporters-of-the-Young-Gallery-Members-Show)

From 13 November see an exhibition showcasing the work of the Supporters of the Young Gallery in Gallery 3.

## VISIT THE STATE ROOMS OF TABLEY HOUSE

See the wonderful historic splendour of Tabley House State Rooms.

Admire the extraordinary collection of art, furniture, and memorabilia and hear about the intriguing history of the Leicester family.

Following on from TURNER 250 – Tabley is exploring further his patron Sir John Flemming Leicester who owned Tabley from 1770 to 1827. 
New displays illustrate Sir John’s own artistic work created as a young man during his Grand Tour of Europe.

> _“The superb collection of paintings, furniture and artefacts were made more interesting by the band of friendly and well informed volunteers.”_

## Tabley House Tea Room

TABLEY TEA ROOM

Tabley House Collection Tea Room offers a range of light refreshments, teas, coffees, freshly made sandwiches, cakes and afternoon teas in a beautiful, peaceful, and historic setting with waitress service at your table.

Situated in the Old Hall Room, the Tea Room links the Grade I listed stately home with the 17th Century St Peter’s Chapel.

The Tea Room opens from 12 noon from Thursday through to Sunday, and is free to enter.

Tel: 077384 06466

For the Tea Room menu click on the link under Visit Us.

## St Peter’s Chapel

St Peter’s Chapel originally built on an island in the Mere in 1678, was moved in 1927 and re-erected on its present site adjacent to the house. The Chapel, has impressive stained glass, with one window designed by Burne-Jones.

The Chapel was recently used as the location for an important wedding scene in BBC’s ‘Peaky Blinders’.

The Chapel is free to enter and is accessed via the Tea Room entrance
